state.hypothesis: Polychlorinated biphenyls and their hydroxylated metabolites disrupt thyroid hormone homeostasis by interfering with thyroid hormone transport proteins and altering circulating thyroid hormone levels.

sentences.0: Background
sentences.1: An increasing number of studies have shown that several ubiquitous environmental contaminants possess thyroid hormone–disrupting capacities.
sentences.10: In a subsample analysis, a negative relationship was also found between maternal PCP levels and cord fT4 concentrations in neonates (β = −0.59, p = 0.02).
sentences.100: Adjustment for lipid content was not done for CPCs because they are bound to plasma proteins.
sentences.101: A bilateral p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
sentences.102: Database management and variable transformation were performed with SPSS (version 2.0; SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA) whereas statistical analyses were conducted with SAS (version 9.1; SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA).
sentences.103: Results
sentences.104: Table 1 lists the characteristics of included and excluded pregnant Inuit women and their infants at birth and at 7 months of age.
sentences.105: Sociodemographic characteristics and exposure to OCs (data not shown) were similar between the pregnant women who were included and and those excluded from the study.
sentences.106: In accordance with the exclusion criteria, newborns included in the study had a longer gestational age and were heavier.
sentences.107: Percentages of breast-feeding at birth and at 7 months of age were significantly greater in infants included than in those excluded.
sentences.108: ere was no significant difference in exposure to OCs between included and excluded infants at birth and at 7 months of age (data not shown).
sentences.109: Table 2 presents descriptive statistics for OCs and CPCs in maternal, cord, and infant plasma.
sentences.11: No association was observed between contaminants and thyroid hormones at 7 months of age.
sentences.110: PCB-153 is the most prevalent congener in this population the mean concentration of PCB-153 was higher in pregnant women, followed by infant and cord plasma levels.
sentences.111: The correlation on a lipid basis between maternal and cord plasma PCB-153 was very high (r = 0.94), but only moderate between maternal and infant concentrations (r = 0.41) and cord and infant concentrations (r = 0.46).
sentences.112: Mean lipid-adjusted HCB concentrations were similar for newborn, infant, and maternal plasma samples.
sentences.113: As for PCB-153, the correlation between maternal and cord plasma HCB was high (r = 0.86), but in the moderate range between maternal and infant concentrations (r = 0.33) and cord and infant concentrations (r = 0.36).
sentences.114: The mean wet weight concentration of HO-PCBs was higher in pregnant women than in cord plasma, and levels were highly intercorrelated (r = 0.96).
sentences.115: Most of the HO-PCBs detected in mothers and newborns were moderately correlated with PCB-153 (r = 0.21–0.78, median: newborn r = 0.63; maternal r = 0.53) on a wet weight basis.
sentences.116: PCP was detected in all maternal and umbilical cord plasma samples.
sentences.117: Levels were higher in umbilical cord than in maternal plasma and were also very highly correlated (r = 0.85).
sentences.118: Intercorrelations of contaminants in maternal, umbilical cord, and infant plasma are also presented in Table 2.
sentences.119: In maternal and cord samples, PCB-153 concentrations were highly correlated with HO-PCBs and moderately with HCB.
sentences.12: Conclusion
sentences.120: Also, PCP was weakly correlated with the other contaminants.
sentences.121: Concentrations of PCB-153 and HCB were highly correlated in infant plasma.
sentences.122: A large proportion of the mothers had TSH values outside the TSH euthyroid reference range (0.4–2.5 mIU/L).
sentences.123: Sixteen percent (n = 20) had TSH concentrations below the lower limit whereas 10% (n =13) had values higher than the reference range.
sentences.124: ere were no significant differences in OC concentrations between mothers outside and within the TSH euthyroid refence range.
sentences.125: Most infants at birth and at 7 months of age had TSH and fT4 levels within the normal range.
sentences.126: The associations between OCs and CPCs and the thyroid parameters documented in pregnant women at delivery are presented in Table 3.
sentences.127: Simple regression models showed a significant positive association between HO-PCBs and T3.
sentences.128: Simple and multiple regressions between contaminants and TSH as well as fT4 were not significant.
sentences.129: Adjustment for confounding factors strengthens the positive association between HO-PCBs and T3.
sentences.13: Overall, there is little evidence that the environmental contaminants analyzed in this study affect thyroid hormone status in Inuit mothers and their infants.
sentences.130: Table 4 shows simple and multiple linear associations between thyroid parameters measured in umbilical cord blood and OCs or CPCs levels in cord and maternal plasma.
sentences.131: In newborns at birth, no significant association was observed between cord blood contaminants and TH concentrations in univariate models.
sentences.132: However, negative associations were found for umbilical cord and maternal PCB-153 with TBG concentrations after control for confounders.
sentences.133: A negative association between cord fT4 and maternal PCP, but not cord PCP, was found before and after controlling for confounders.
sentences.134: In the subsample analysis of cord CPC, characteristics of newborns included were similar, except that those included had a higher birth weight (included: mean = 3,758 g, excluded: mean = 3,508 g, p = 0.006).
sentences.135: Also, in the subsample analysis of maternal CPC, characteristics of mothers and newborns were similar, except that maternal and cord Se concentrations were lower (mothers included: mean = 1.09 μmol/L, excluded: mean = 1.44 μmol/L, p = 0.01; newborns included: mean = 3.11 μmol/L, excluded: mean = 3.84 μmol/L, p = 0.04).
sentences.136: Concentrations of T3 in cord blood were not associated with any of the contaminants under study.
sentences.137: A significant negative association between PCB-153 and TSH was obtained in simple linear regression for infants 7 months of age (Table 5).
sentences.138: However, the association was no longer significant after adjustment for breast-feeding status.
sentences.139: Interaction terms between OCs and breast-feeding status were not significant.
sentences.14: The possibility that PCP may decrease thyroxine levels in neonates requires further investigation.
sentences.140: The associations were not significant after stratification for breast-feeding status (data not shown).
sentences.141: Discussion
sentences.142: In the present study, we investigated the potential negative effects of OCs and CPCs on the circulating concentrations of TH among Inuit women and their infants.
sentences.143: Overall, the results show that plasma concentration of OCs and CPCs were not significant predictors of TSH and TH concentrations in this population of pregnant women and their offspring.
sentences.144: However, maternal levels of PCP were negatively associated with fT4 concen- trations in umbilical cord blood of neonates, suggesting that this compound may reduce the transfer of maternal T4 across the placenta to the developing fetus.
sentences.145: As reported in most studies [reviewed by ], an association between PCB-153 and TH concentrations was not found in Inuit neonates at birth.
sentences.146: Similarly, no association was seen in these infants at the 7-months follow-up.
sentences.147: Also, these data did not corroborate the relationship between PCB congeners and TSH or TH levels seen in the CHAMACOS (Center for the Health Assessment of Mothers and Children of Salinas) study, in any of the exposure matrices (maternal, cord, or infant plasma).
sentences.148: ese associations were observed even though the maternal PCB-153 concentrations were almost 20 times lower than those in the present study.
sentences.149: Difference in the profile of other PCB congeners in that population may provide one explanation for the discrepancy in results between the CHAMACOS study and the present study.
sentences.15: Tyroid hormones (TH) play several essential roles for brain maturation in humans.
sentences.150: Another possible important difference between both populations is the iodine intake.
sentences.151: Indeed, iodine, which is essential for thyroid function, is found in high concentration in some seafood products.
sentences.152: erefore, exposure to iodine and OCs co-occurs in individuals such as the Nunavik Inuit, who consume a large amount of marine products.
sentences.153: Therefore, not taking into account urinary iodine concentrations in epidemiologic studies aiming to investigate this research question may partly explain the inconsistent results.
sentences.154: The absence of an association between HCB and umbilical cord fT4 concentrations in this study are not consistent with a previous finding of significant positive associations in another sample of Inuit neonates and in newborns from the Lower North Shore of the St. Lawrence River.
sentences.155: The lower statistical power of the present study as well as a difference in adjustment of confounders may account for the differential results.
sentences.156: However, the absence of relationship between HCB and fT4 found in the present study are in agreement with two other epidemiologic studies among neonates.
sentences.157: The absence of an association between PCB-153 and thyroid parameters in pregnant Inuit women was similar to that reported in the second Faroe Islands cohort.
sentences.158: However, two other epidemiologic studies among pregnant women found a significant negative association of PCBs with T3 and/or tT4 status whereas, among Mexican-American pregnant women, three PCB congeners (44, 52, and 183) were negatively related to fT4 concentrations.
sentences.159: It is possible that the effects observed in these three studies were mostly attributable to the exposure to polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and polychlorinated dibenzofurans, which are usually higher in urban settings than in isolated populations mostly exposed to environmental contaminants through fish and marine mammal consumption.
sentences.16: Adequate levels are necessary at specific times in certain regions of the brain for the normal development of the nervous system during fetal and neonatal periods.
sentences.160: As previously mentioned, high dietary iodine intake in fish-eating populations may also explain the lack of association between PCB-153 and thyroid hormone status in mothers.
sentences.161: HCB body burden was not associated with thyroid hormone profile in Inuit pregnant women at delivery.
sentences.162: Two other studies investigated whether exposure to low background concentrations of HCB was related to TH levels during pregnancy.
sentences.163: An inverse relationship between plasma HCB concentrations and T3 levels was reported among Canadians, and negative associations between HCB concentrations and fT4 and tT4 levels were found in the CHAMACOS study.
sentences.164: However, the authors were not able to determine whether effects on TH concentrations were related to PCBs or HCB plasma concentrations because these exposures were highly correlated.
sentences.165: In the present study we also documented concentrations of HO-PCBs and PCP because several in vitro studies have revealed their potency in competitively inhibiting T4 binding to TTR.
sentences.166: This T4-binding protein is implicated in the delivery of maternal T4 to the fetus across the placenta as well as the transport of T4 from blood into cerebrospinal fluid during brain maturation.
sentences.167: However, experiments with TTR-null mice have shown that TTR is not essential for T4 distribution in brain.
sentences.168: Nevertheless, as would be predicted from toxicologic data, a negative association was found between maternal PCP plasma concentrations and umbilical cord fT4 levels, but not with umbilical cord PCP, which has two times the binding affinity of the natural ligand T4 for TTR.
sentences.169: Moreover, it was the predominant CPC in the Inuit population, and concentrations were mostly higher in umbilical cord plasma than in maternal plasma.
sentences.17: Maternal TH are the only source of TH for the developing brain of the fetus during the first trimester of pregnancy, at the end of which the fetal hypothalamic–pituitary system initiates its own TH synthesis and secretion.
sentences.170: Taken together, these findings seem to indicate that PCP may impede the transfer of maternal T4 to the fetus across the placental barrier to a certain extent by inhibiting maternal T4 binding to TTR.
sentences.171: is mechanism may also have favored the transport of maternal PCP to the fetal circulation, which may explain the higher concentration of this compound in cord blood compared with maternal blood.
sentences.172: The relation between maternal PCP and neonate fT4 concentrations was no longer evident at the later age, because there was no association between maternal or cord PCP and fT4 levels when the infants were 7 months of age (data not shown).
sentences.173: The rapid maturation of the hypothalamus–pituitary–thyroid axis after the severing of the umbilical cord, which leads to the complete independence of the newborn from a maternal source of fT4, may explain such findings.
sentences.174: However, these results should be interpreted with caution because no association was found with cord blood PCP concentrations even though they were highly correlated with maternal PCP levels (r = 0.85).
sentences.176: Se concentrations of mothers and newborns included in the subsample analysis were lower than in the sample used for OCs (n = 80).
sentences.177: Two other epidemiologic studies have looked at the association between CPC and TH concentrations in neonates.
sentences.178: In another sample of Inuit newborns, found a negative correlation between the sum of PCP and 14 HO-PCBs with cord fT4, whereas reported a positive correlation between 6 HO-PCBs and neonatal blood-spot fT4 obtained on a filter paper.
sentences.179: Other studies are needed to ascertain the potential effects of CPCs on neonatal TH concentrations, because the small sample size in the present study limits its conclusions.
sentences.18: Studies have demonstrated that maternal TH can regulate gene expression in the fetal cortex, but their action on the developing brain remains unclear.
sentences.180: The increase of T3 with concentrations of HO-PCBs in pregnant women may be attributable to selective or combined inhibition of sulfotransferase and type I deiodinase (D1) activities, as these metabolites have been shown to competitively inhibit D1 and diiodothyronine sulfotransferases actions.
sentences.181: Indeed, in adults, sulfotransferases irreversibly inactivate TH actions and facilitate D1 deiodination for complete degradation in the liver.
sentences.182: Interestingly, in fetuses sulfated T4 and T3 are elevated compared with adult concentrations and have been proposed to serve as a reservoir of inactive TH for subsequent activation by sulfotransferases at specific developmental stages.
sentences.183: is difference in TH metabolism between fetuses and adults, especially for sulfotransferase and deiodinase activities, may explain the absence of HO-PCB effects on cord T3 compared with maternal T3.
sentences.184: These findings suggest that the synthesis or metabolism of transport proteins may be affected by environmental contaminants.
sentences.185: Indeed, the negative association between PCB-153 and serum TBG concentration could by mediated by a diminution of TBG synthesis by the liver.

sentences.188: Most toxicologic studies have focused on the competitive binding assessment of environmental contaminants with T4, without evaluating their ability to modify transport protein synthesis.
sentences.189: Consequently, the results cannot be corroborated on biological mechanisms because toxicologic data are unavailable.

sentences.2: Prenatal exposure to some of them, such as polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), has also been associated with adverse neurodevelopmental effects in infants.
sentences.20: Prenatal exposure to polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), a group of persistent and lipophilic organochlorine compounds (OCs), has been associated with neurodevelopmental deficits in childhood in most cohort studies focusing on developmental neurotoxicity of PCBs.
sentences.200: Nevertheless, epidemiologic studies of pregnant women suffering from hypothyroxinemia (low fT4) have shown that reduced transfer of maternal fT4 during fetal brain maturation can negatively affect the neurocognitive function in infants.
sentences.201: Results from the neurodevelopment assessment of the participating infants in this cohort will allow us to determine whether a reduction of fT4 concentrations during fetal development, perhaps mediated by PCP, may induce deficits similar to those observed in the offspring of hypothyroxinemic pregnant women.
sentences.21: Animals studies have reported detrimental effects of in utero exposure to PCBs on cognitive and motor functions as well as on the auditory system.
sentences.22: At the biochemical level, several PCB congeners disrupt the thyroid function, principally by lowering plasma thyroxine (T4) and greatly depressing T4 concentrations in brain tissue in rats exposed prenatally.
sentences.23: Hexachlorobenzene (HCB) has been used as a fungicide and is also a by-product of the manufacturing of chlorinated solvents and metallurgical processes.
sentences.24: HCB is found worldwide because of its long-range atmospheric transport, is very persistent, and tends to accumulate in adipose tissues.
sentences.25: Exposure to HCB in rats can produce several effects including reduced T4 plasma levels and hypothyroidism.
sentences.26: HCB has been shown to interfere with T4 uptake into the cerebrospinal fluid in rats.
sentences.27: Transport of T4 across the blood–brain barrier by transthyretin (TTR) is one mechanism by which TH reaches the developing fetal brain and also facilitates maternal transfer across the placenta.
sentences.28: Some chlorinated phenolic compounds (CPC) such as the hydroxylated metabolites of PCBs (HO-PCBs) and pentachlorophenol (PCP) possess a greater in vitro binding affinity for TTR than the natural ligand T4. Furthermore, HO-PCBs and PCP can strongly inhibit TH sulfation, which along with desulfation appear to be very important pathways regulating circulating TH concentrations in the fetus.
sentences.29: Results from epidemiologic studies among pregnant women are scarce, but suggest potential effects of OCs on thyroid economy.
sentences.3: Objectives
sentences.30: In contrast, assessments of the relation between environmental contaminants and the thyroid status of newborns have resulted in equivocal findings, possibly because of differences in the biological matrices for exposure determination (blood, plasma, placenta, or breast milk), the contaminants measured, and the congener grouping as well as the timing of postnatal TH dosage.
sentences.31: With regard to CPCs, only two studies have investigated their effects in newborns and found opposite results.
sentences.32: Because the potential effects of thyroid-disrupting contaminants on maternal and neonatal thyroid status are not yet clear, we undertook a study to determine the relationship of background exposure to OCs and CPCs with TH status in pregnant women and their infants within the first year of the infant’s life.
sentences.33: This study addresses this research question among the Inuit population of Nunavik because these communities are among the most heavily exposed to these contaminants on earth, mainly through sea mammal consumption.
sentences.34: Materials and Methods
sentences.35: Population
sentences.36: Nunavik is the northern region of Québec where approximately 9,500 Inuit live in 14 communities on the coast of the Hudson and Ungava Bays.
sentences.37: All pregnant Inuit women from the three largest communities of the Hudson Bay coast of Nunavik were invited to participate in a study that aimed to document the effects of prenatal exposure to environmental contaminants on infant development.
sentences.38: From November 1995 to March 2001, a research assistant contacted each potential participant after her first prenatal visit with a midwife or a nurse.
sentences.39: All pregnant women gave informed consent for themselves and for their infants before participating in the study.
sentences.4: In this study we examined the relationship between exposure to potential thyroid hormone–disrupting toxicants and thyroid hormone status in pregnant Inuit women from Nunavik and their infants within the first year of life.
sentences.40: The study protocol was approved by the Nunavik Nutrition and Health Committee and by ethics committees at Laval University (Québec City, Québec, Canada) and Wayne State University (Detroit, Michigan).
sentences.41: One prenatal and two postnatal (at 1 and 6 months) interviews were conducted to obtain sociodemographic and personal information from the mothers.
sentences.42: The participation rate for this study was 69%.
sentences.43: Among the 248 participating mother–infant dyads, 17.8% were excluded due to the adoption of the newborn, fetal or postnatal mortality, and loss to follow-up.
sentences.44: Biological data on TH and OC concentrations were available for 204 pregnant women.
sentences.45: Because TH levels slowly return to non-pregnancy levels after delivery and to ensure that measured levels of TH were not related to postpartum thyroid dysfunction, which occurs between 2 and 12 months postpartum, mothers from whom the blood sample was drawn 31 days after delivery were excluded from the statistical analysis (n = 71).
sentences.46: Pregnant women who declared using medication for thyroid diseases were also excluded (n = 4).
sentences.47: Biological data on TH and OC concentrations were available for 108 infants at birth and 175 infants at 7 months of age.
sentences.48: Neonates born prematurely and/or with low birth weight were also excluded because transient neonatal hypothyroxinemia may be induced by prematurity (< 37 weeks gestation, n = 6) and low birth weight (< 2,500 g, n = 1).
sentences.49: Blood sampling and laboratory procedures
sentences.5: Methods
sentences.50: A 12.5-mL blood sample was collected from participating women at delivery or within the subsequent weeks (median = 2 days).
sentences.51: A 30-mL blood sample was collected from the umbilical cord after it was severed, and a 5-mL blood sample was obtained at 7 months postpartum (median = 6.9 months).
sentences.52: OC, CPC, and TH levels were measured in maternal, cord, and infant plasma.
sentences.53: Selenium and plasma lipid concentrations were also measured in samples for confounding assessment.
sentences.54: Blood samples were collected in vials containing EDTA as the anticoagulant and centrifuged (10 min, 5,000 rpm), and the plasma transferred into glass vials prewashed with hexane.
sentences.55: Plasma samples were frozen at −80°C until time of analysis.
sentences.56: We measured concentrations of the 14 most frequently detected PCB congeners in human populations [IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) nos. 28, 52, 99, 101, 105, 118, 128, 138, 153, 156, 170, 180, 183, 187] and HCB in the purified extracts using an HP-5890 series II gas chromatograph (Hewlett-Packard, Palo Alto, CA, USA) equipped with dual-capillary columns (HP Ultra and Ultra II; Hewlett-Packard) and dual Ni-63 electron capture detectors (Hewlett-Packard).
sentences.57: Detailed laboratory procedures and quality control procedures for OCs were described previously by and, respectively.
sentences.58: Limits of detection for OCs were 0.02 μg/L.
sentences.59: We determined concentrations of CPCs by extracting the plasma samples on an Oasis HLB (540 mg; Waters Corp., Milford, MA, USA) solid phase extraction column according to a modified method by.
sentences.6: We measured thyroid hormone parameters [thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (fT4), total triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG)] and concentrations of several contaminants [PCB-153, hydroxylated metabolites of PCBs (HO-PCBs), pentachlorophenol (PCP) and hexachlorobenzene (HCB)] in maternal plasma at delivery (n = 120), in umbilical cord plasma (n = 95), and in infant plasma at 7 months postpartum (n = 130).
sentences.60: Extraction and cleanup were completed on a Zymark Rapidtrace Automated SPE workstation (Zymark Corp., Hopkinton, MA, USA).
sentences.61: CPCs were eluted with dichloromethane:methanol (9:1) in a third fraction on a prepacked Florisil column (1 g; Alltech, Lexington, KY, USA).
sentences.62: After evaporation, the compounds were derivatized using diazomethane in hexane according to the method of.
sentences.63: The derivatized fraction was then cleaned up on an activated silica/acidic silica column before evaporation, addition of recovery standard, and quantification by gas chromatography/high resolution mass spectrometry.
sentences.64: HO-PCB results are presented as a sum of the 11 major HO-PCBs (4-HO-CB-107, 3-HO-CB-153, 4-HO-CB-146, 3′-HO-CB-138, 4-HO-CB-163, 4-HO-CB-187, 4-HO-CB-202, 4′-HO-CB-172, 4-HO-CB-193, 4′-HO-CB-199, and 4-HO-CB-208).
sentences.65: The limit of detection for those compounds varied between 2 and 6 ng/L.
sentences.66: We determined total cholesterol, free cholesterol, and triglycerides in plasma by standard enzymatic procedures, whereas we quantified phospholipids according to using a commercial kit (Wako Pure Chemical Industries, Richmond, VA, USA).
sentences.67: Concentrations of total plasma lipids were estimated according to the formula developed by.
sentences.68: Blood Se concentrations were determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (PE Elan 6000; PerkinElmer Sciex, Concord, ON, Canada).
sentences.69: The limit of detection for blood Se was 0.1 μmol/L.
sentences.7: Results
sentences.70: We analyzed serum throid-stimulating hormone (TSH), free T4 (fT4), total triiodothyronine (T3), and thyroid-binding globulin (TBG), the major transport protein of TH, using radioimmunoassay methods.
sentences.71: TSH, fT4, and T3 were measured on the Bayer Immuno 1 System (Bayer Corp., Tarrytown, NY, USA).
sentences.72: TBG was determined on the Clinical Assays GammaDab system commercialized by DiaSorin (Stillwater, MN, USA).
sentences.73: Statistical analysis
sentences.74: Contaminant concentrations and thyroid parameters were all log-transformed to satisfy criteria of normality.
sentences.75: We used Pearson correlations to evaluate relations between contaminants, and simple and multiple linear regression models to evaluate the relationship between environmental contaminants, TH, and TBG in plasma.
sentences.76: A value equal to half the limit of detection of the analytical method was attributed to nondetected contaminants in biological samples.
sentences.77: Only PCB congeners with a detection frequency of at least 70% were considered.
sentences.78: We evaluated exposure to PCB by several approaches.
sentences.79: First, all PCB congeners were evaluated individually.
sentences.8: In pregnant women, we found a positive association between HO-PCBs and T3 concentrations (β = 0.57, p = 0.02).
sentences.80: Second, congeners were grouped according to their dioxin-like activity or their capacity to induce the microsomal enzymes UDP-GT (uridine diphosphate-glucuronosyl transferase), CYP1A (cytochrome P4501A), and CYP2B as proposed by.
sentences.81: For the later grouping, the enzyme-inducing congeners included were PCBs 99, 118, 153, 180, and 187.
sentences.82: Third, because all PCB congeners were highly correlated in the study population, PCB-153 was selected as a marker of exposure to all PCBs.
sentences.83: Indeed, in maternal plasma, intercorrelations among PCB congeners varied from 0.62 to 0.96.
sentences.84: Similarly, in cord and infant plasma, intercorrelations among PCB congeners varied from 0.73 to 0.98 and 0.81 to 0.99, respectively.
sentences.85: Correlations between PCB-153 and the sum of PCB inducers in maternal, cord, and infant plasma were all 0.99.
sentences.86: Because results obtained using all PCB congeners or groupings did not change significantly from those obtained with PCB-153 (data not shown), only results for PCB-153 are presented.
sentences.87: We performed simple regressions between potential confounding variables and thyroid parameters to determine which covariate should be included in multiple linear regression analyses.
sentences.88: Covariates associated at a p-value ≤ 0.10 were included in multiple regression models to assess their confounding influence.
sentences.89: Covariates modifying the regression coefficient of the contaminants by > 10% with any of the TH were included in adjusted models for all TH parameters.
sentences.9: In umbilical cord blood, PCB-153 concentrations were negatively associated with TBG levels (β = −0.26, p = 0.01).
sentences.90: The following covariates were evaluated in pregnant women: age at delivery, prepregnancy body weight, socioeconomic status [Hollingshead Index of Social Status (Hollingshead AB, unpublished data)], alcohol and cigarette consumption, fish consumption during pregnancy, and plasma Se concentration.
sentences.91: Because age at delivery and parity were highly intercorrelated, only the former was retained in the multiple models, where appropriate, because it was a better predictor of TH concentrations in pregnant women.
sentences.92: Nine women were not included in statistical analysis because of absence of information regarding alcohol consumption.
sentences.93: Most variables evaluated as potential confounders in newborns were also tested in the models at 7 months of age.
sentences.94: The primary caregiver’s score for socioeconomic status, maternal alcohol and cigarette consumption, maternal fish consumption during pregnancy, sex, breast-feeding status, as well as Se level in cord blood were tested for confounding at both ages.
sentences.95: Gestational age and birth weight were also highly intercorrelated in newborns.
sentences.96: erefore, only the former was included in multiple regression models, where appropriate, because it was a better predictor of TH concentrations.
sentences.97: Six newborns were excluded due to unmeasured cord selenium concentrations, and 15 infants were excluded for lack of information regarding breast-feeding status.
sentences.98: Because breast-feeding is an important source of postnatal exposure, an interaction term between OC concentrations and breast-feeding status at 7 months of age was also tested in multiple regression models.
sentences.99: Statistical models assessing the relationship between the lipophilic contaminants PCB-153 or HCB and thyroid parameters were further adjusted for total plasma lipid concentrations because have shown that this approach is less prone to estimate bias compared with lipid standardization.

state.hypothesis: Inorganic lead and organic lead cause distinct neurotoxic effects and clinical syndromes, despite both disrupting GABA and glutamate neurotransmitter systems.

sentences.0: Comparative Observations on Inorganic and Organic Lead Neurotoxicity by M. Anthony Verity* Environmental and occupational exposure to lead still generates concern, and recent studies have focused such concern on the role of body burden of lead during the fetal/neonatal period, especially in the genesis of disturbed central nervous system development.
sentences.1: This discussion provides some comparative observations on the neurotoxicity of inorganic and organic lead species.
sentences.10: "Recommendation 14-52: ... [chemical agents] special attention should be given to the evaluation of effects on the fetus, .iifnt... .uniquely vuinerable to environmental toxicants which damage the CNS."
sentences.100: Prolonga- tion of neuronal survival in culture is dependent on chronic depolarization usually maintained by high extracellular K+ (61-63).
sentences.101: How depolarization affects neuronal survival and differentiation is unclear but increased [K+]e is known to activate voltage-sensitive Ca2+ channels (64), and Ca2+ entry has been implicated in the developmental effects of depolarization on neuronal survival and differentiation.
sentences.102: Pb2+ uptake may occur via calcium channels (65).
sentences.103: Simons and Pocock (65), using chromaffin cels, demonstrated an approx- imate 5-fold stimulation of Pb2+ uptake following K+ de- polarization, which was antagonized by external Ca2+ inhib- ited by Ca2+ channel blockers and stimulated by the Ca2+ agonist BAY K8644 (Table 4).
sentences.104: More specifically, Gabo et al. (66) studied the role of depolrization on the survival and differentiation of cerebellar granule cells in culture and found that neuronal survival was not influenced by the bioelectric activity but was critically dependent on the depolarization-induced transmembrane Ca2+ flux (Table 5).
sentences.105: Moreover, inhibitors of calmodulin blocked the differentiating effect of K+-induced depolarization.
sentences.106: These observations link the survival and differentiation of neurons to a constant depolarization-coupled Ca2+ flux, Table 4.
sentences.107: Pb2+ uptake occurs via Ca2, channels (65).
sentences.108: itself transduced by a calmodulin-dependent event(s) to neuronal differentiation, especially neurite outgrowth, speci- fication, and stabilization of synaptic contacts.
sentences.109: A critical deter- minant of neurite organization is microtubule assembly regu- lated by the calmodulin-Ca2+ complex (67)(68)(69).
sentences.11: Introduction
sentences.110: How then can we explain the apparent differences in brain injury resulting from acute contrasted to low-level, chronic inorganic Pb2+ intoxication?
sentences.111: In the acute model we may propose that Pb2+ uptake via Ca2+ channels (voltage sensi- tive and insensitive) into immature capillary endothelial cells will trigger intracellular processes leading to defective mito- chondrial bioenergetics and mobilization of intracellular Ca2+, leading to cellular (endothelial) necrosis.
sentences.112: In contrast, low-level, chronic Pb2+ exposure is manifested by subtle defects in axodendritic architecture and neurite organization secondary to defective cytoskeletal organization.
sentences.113: The need for continued depolarization in neuronal development is linked to stimulation of Pb2+ uptake and the resultant high-affinity binding to Ca2+ binding proteins, especially calmodulin.
sentences.114: The abnormal and possibly prolonged activation of calmodulin-dependent processes, especially the activation of protein kinase C, will lead to distorted transmembrane signalling and defective neuronal differentiation (Table 6).
sentences.115: The author acknowledges the financial support of the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences and numerous discussions with many coileagues including S. Bondy, L. Chang, M. Cheung, G. Goldstein, D. Holzman, T. Sara- fian, E. Silbergeld, and H. Tilson.
sentences.116: The editorial assistance of S. Brooks is gratefully appreciated.
sentences.12: Lead exposure from environmental and occupational sources still remains of great concern.
sentences.13: Although low-level amounts of lead are present in man and all living organisms, indices of sublethal health effects and the nature of lead speciation are problems of recurrent concern.

state.hypothesis: Urinary 1-naphthol and 2-naphthol concentrations are quantitative biomarkers of occupational naphthalene exposure.

sentences.0: Urinary naphthols as an indicator of exposure to naphthalene
sentences.1: Urinary naphthols as an indicator of exposure to naphthalene
sentences.10: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (1) has determined that naphthalene is not classifiable as a carcinogen to humans.
sentences.100: The biological monitoring of naphthalene provides a better estimation of the adsorbed substances than measurements of the corresponding contaminates in air because the skin can be the main route of exposure (16).
sentences.101: Naphthalene metabolism is complex and leads to the formation of a wide assortment of hydroxylated derivatives, quinones, and conjugates of glucuronic acid, glutathione, and sulfate (24).
sentences.102: Immunological techniques are being developed for the identification of naphthalene mercapturic acid derivatives in urine (25) and naphthalene hemoglobin adducts in blood (26).
sentences.103: Traditionally, the most common method used for the biological monitoring of naphthalene exposure has been based on measuring a metabolite of naphthalene, usually urinary I-naphthol.
sentences.104: Some caution must be exercised in using 1-naphthol as a biomarker of naphthalene exposure in the general population because this metabolite is also excreted after exposure to the common insecticide carbaryl (27).
sentences.105: Investigations by Connor et a1 (28) have shown that smoking can contribute to the excretion of 1naphthol in urine.
sentences.106: Recent studies have demonstrated that the maximum concentration of 1-naphthol in the urine of operators working with the naphthalene oil distillation process appears 1 h after the end of a shift (15).
sentences.107: The 1naphthol concentration was the highest in the morning before the workday.
sentences.108: Measurements taken at this time of day probably reflect the exposure on the previous day (16).
sentences.109: The present study attempted to evaluate the relation between naphthalene exposure and various recently developed biomarkers so that a biological exposure index corresponding to naphthalene exposure can be estimated.
sentences.11: The most common hematologic effect in humans following the ingestion of naphthalene is hemolytic anemia (3,8) and hepatic and neurological effects (8).
sentences.110: Our results show that most naphthalene is metabolized to 1-and 2-naphthol and 1,4-naphthoquinone (figure 2).
sentences.111: Small amounts of 1-naphthol and 2-naphthol are excreted in the urine after the dermal application of naphthalene (4).
sentences.112: In an earlier study it has been shown that there is a good statistical correlation between 1-naphthol excretion and naphthalene exposure in the concelltration range of 0.2-6 mg/m3.
sentences.113: This urinary metabolite can indicate exposure to both naphthalene and low concentrations of 1-naphthol during the naphthalene oil distillation process (15).
sentences.114: Our study confirms a previous assumption that there is a correlation between the presence of naphthalene in air and the urinary excretion of 1-naphthol and 2-naphthol, which are two major oxygenated metabolites of naphthalene.
sentences.115: Significant correlations between I-naph-tho1 or 2-naphthol and naphthalene exposure (figures 3 and 4) were found.
sentences.116: It is important to stress that the present study was cassied out among workers in a coke plant.
sentences.117: The workers were exposed to numerous other volatile compounds in addition to naphthalene (figure 1).
sentences.118: Several aromatic hydrocarbons in tar and naphthalene oil are known to have either synergistic or antagonistic effects on coexposure to naphthalene.
sentences.119: The GC-MS analysis of breathing-zone air showed that the coke plant workers employed in the naphthalene oil distillation process are simultaneously exposed to naphthalene, 1 -and 2-methylnaphthalenes, dimethylnaphthalene isomers, trimethylnaphthalene (figure 1) and other compounds (Bieniek & Kurkiewicz, unpublished results).
sentences.12: The metabolism of naphthalene has been studied in experimental animals (7,(9)(10)(11)(12).
sentences.120: In conclusion, our results show the existence of low exposure to naphthalene, which is however qualitatively diversified in coke plants.
sentences.121: Urinary 1-naphthol and 2naphthol seem to be useful biomarkers in the assessment of naphthalene exposure in a coke plant.

sentences.126: I would like to thank the Managing Board of the Zabrze Cokery Plant for their kind permission to continue my research and Mr S Kurkiewicz and Ms K Klimek for their kind help in the GC-MS measurements and statistical analyses.
sentences.13: Little information is available pertaining to the metabolism of naphthalene by humans.
sentences.14: Naphthalene is effectively metabolized to the toxic compound naphthoquinone (7,13) and 1,2-dihydro-l,2-naphthalenediol( 14).
sentences.15: An earlier report presented what appeared to be a case of oral ingestion in which the urine of an 18-month-old child was found to contain 1naphthol, 2-naphthol, 1,2-naphthoquinone, and 1,4-naphthoquinone (1 3).

sentences.19: Increased urinary levels of 1-naphthol have been measured in several environments for iron foundry workers (IS), coke plant workers (15), and assemblers handling creosote-impregnated wood (16).

sentences.10: Our results revealed that the discarding of wastes into the open dump is a potential source of soil contamination in the immediate vicinity and beyond, via dispersal.

sentences.103: The wastes in the open dump were predominantly domestic, agricultural, and industrial waste materials trucked down to the location.

sentences.105: The open dump is now in the vicinity of the Muledane residential housing estate and poses a potential health threat to the residents.
sentences.106: The choice of the determined potential contaminants – phthalate esters and metals (lead, cadmium, manganese, zinc, iron and calcium) – was informed by the nature of wastes in the site.

state.hypothesis: The fast acetylator phenotype of NAT2 increases the risk of colorectal cancer in individuals with high dietary intake of red meat, particularly when the meat is cooked in ways that generate high levels of carcinogens.

sentences.0: Background
sentences.1: Diet contributes significantly to colorectal cancer (CRC) aetiology and may be potentially modifiable.
sentences.10: Low meat intake in the studied populations may influence the result.
sentences.100: Dietary antioxidants such as vitamin C, vitamin E and carotene may reduce DNA alkylation by acting as nitrosation inhibitors.
sentences.101: O6-Methyl-guanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGTM) is the DNA repair enzyme responsible for the cellular defence against alkylation damage in human cells.
sentences.102: Possible interactions of MGTM Ile143Val polymorphism and these antioxidants were assessed in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)-Norfolk cohort.
sentences.103: Low intake of vitamin C, vitamin E and carotene intake was associated with a 27%, 46% and 43% higher risk of CRC respectively among carriers of the variant genotype compared with homozygous wildtype carriers with low intake (reference) (P-interaction 0.12, 0.009 and 0.005 respectively).
sentences.104: In contrast, participants with high intake of vitamin C, vitamin E and carotene were not at risk of CRC.
sentences.105: These results suggest that individuals with genetically determined low DNA repair capacity are at a high risk of CRC by low intake of vitamin C, vitamin E and carotene.
sentences.106: High intake of calcium and vitamin D has been inversely related to colorectal cancer.
sentences.107: The vitamin D receptor (VDR), a nuclear hormone receptor, is essential for the action of vitamin D and calcium.
sentences.108: A functional VDR start codon polymorphism (Fok1) results in a less effective enzyme encoded by the f variant allele compared with the F wildtype allele [43].
sentences.109: This polymorphism was assessed in conjunction with D vitamin in a prospective Chinese cohort of 217 cases and 890 controls.
sentences.11: Interactions between meat, cruciferous vegetables, fibres, calcium, vitamins, and alcohol and ABCB1,NFKB1,GSTM1, GSTT1, CCND1, VDR, MGTM, IL10 and PPARG are suggested.
sentences.110: Although not significant, risk of colorectal cancer tended to be high among homozygous VDR variant genotypes with low intake of calcium in contrast to no change in risk by high intake of calcium (reference: homozygous wildtype genotype) (P-interaction 0.07).
sentences.111: Also, a case–control study assessed the possible interaction between dietary intake of calcium and VDR polymorphisms in 2306 CRC cases and 2749 controls.
sentences.112: The Bsm 1 and poly A VDR polymorphisms were evaluated.
sentences.113: A significant 40% reduction in risk of rectal cancer was observed for the low-activity-associated homozygous VDR LL or bb genotypes when calcium intake was high (OR: 0.56, 95% CI: 0.36–0.85) (reference: homozygous VDR LL or bb genotypes and low calcium intake), whereas the observed risk for the homozygous SS or BB genotypes did not depend on calcium intake (P-interaction 0.01).
sentences.114: No significant interactions were found for colon cancer.
sentences.115: Together, these two studies might suggest that a high intake of calcium can overcome the risk conferred by a deficient VDR.
sentences.116: Alcohol
sentences.117: In a study of the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health cohort, interaction between PPARG Pro12Ala and alcohol intake was found.
sentences.118: Carriers of the variant allele of PPARG Pro12Ala were at increased risk of alcohol-related colorectal cancer (IRR 1.22 pr.10 g alcohol/day, 95% CI: 1.07–1.39), whereas homozygous wildtype Pro-allele carriers were not.
sentences.119: The underlying mechanism of action was recently elucidated.
sentences.12: Conclusions
sentences.120: Hormone replacement therapy is a risk factor for breast cancer, but seems to be associated with lowered risk of colorectal cancer.
sentences.121: PPARγ is a negative regulator of the blood level of female sex hormones (via aromatase activity).
sentences.122: Alcohol, in turn, inactivates PPARγ, leading to increased blood levels of female sex hormones.
sentences.123: The PPARG Pro12Ala amino acid substitution abolishes the alcohol-specific regulation of PPARG presumably by modifying the interaction with the cofactor PGC-1α.
sentences.124: The interaction has not been reproduced for other CRC cohorts, but the finding is indirectly supported by the fact that interaction between PPARG Pro12Ala and alcohol intake was also found in relation to breast cancer.,
sentences.125: Diet and Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer)
sentences.126: Lynch syndrome is caused by germline defects in one of the DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes.
sentences.127: A Dutch case–control study of 145 cases and 103 tumour-free controls with known or suspected Lynch syndrome found an inverse association between fruit intake and CRC (OR: 0.4 for highest vs. lowest tertile, 95% CI: 0.2–0.9).
sentences.128: Diet and epigenetic control of gene expression
sentences.129: Epigenetic modifications (DNA methylation, histone modifications and noncoding RNAs) have a fundamental role in the regulation of gene expression.
sentences.13: A number of interactions between genetic variation and diet are suggested, but the findings need replication in independent, prospective, and well-characterised cohorts before conclusions regarding the underlying biological mechanisms can be reached.
sentences.130: Dietary folate (from green leaves) is the main source of methyl group necessary for DNA synthesis and DNA methylation.
sentences.131: Prospective studies found that low dietary intake of folate and high alcohol consumption were associated with promoter hypermethylation of tumour suppressor genes and genome-wide DNA hypomethylation in CRC tissue from 122 and 609 patients respectively.
sentences.132: Such modulations are considered to lead to inactivation of tumour suppressor genes and activation of oncogenes.
sentences.133: A causal relationship between folate, alcohol and methylation changes was supported by animal studies.,
sentences.134: A subset of CRC patients are characterised by methylation abnormalities in a large number of genes (CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP)).
sentences.135: MTHFR encodes the methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase, which enables the utilisation of methyl groups for DNA synthesis.
sentences.136: A high risk of CIMP-CRC was observed among MTHFR A1298C variant allele carriers with low intake of folate and methionine and high alcohol intake (OR: 2.1, 95% CI: 1.3–3.4), which was in contrast to variant allele carriers with high intake of folate and methionine and low alcohol intake (OR: 1.0, 95% CI: 0.5–1.8) in a case–control study of 916 cases and 1972 controls (P-interaction 0.03) (reference: homozygous wildtype genotype).
sentences.137: This result may suggest that the risk associated with carrying the MTHFR A1298C variant allele can be overcome by a high intake of folate and methionine and low alcohol intake.
sentences.138: A recent meta-analysis found inverse association between blood selenium level and CRC in men.
sentences.139: Although no human studies on selenium and epigenetic in relation to CRC were found, a causal relationship may be suggested by animal and colon cancer cell studies finding that selenium deficiency leads to DNA methylation abnormalities and that selenium supplementation suppressed aberrant DNA methylation.
sentences.14: When the above criteria are met, studies on diet–gene interactions may contribute valuable insight into the biological mechanisms underlying the role of various dietary items in colorectal carcinogenesis.

sentences.33: Statistical analysis

sentences.36: The uncertainties and 95% confidence intervals were assessed by a bootstrap approach in which odds ratios were calculated from each of 8000 bootstrap samples.
sentences.37: The binomial error was accommodated by a binomial resampling of the number of case from the total number of case and controls within each combination of meat intake and polymorphism.

state.hypothesis: Exposure to industrial chemicals used in the manufacture of synthetic chemicals increases the risk of respiratory system cancers in humans.

sentences.0: Excess Lung Cancer Risk in a Synthetic Chemicals Plant by
sentences.1: Excess Lung Cancer Risk in a Synthetic Chemicals Plant by
sentences.10: Our previously published (1) retrospective cohort mortality study of workers exposed to vinyl chlo- ride monomer (VCM) at a synthetic chemicals plant demonstrated an excess risk of death from respiratory system cancer in addition to the already recognized association between VCM exposure and angiosarcoma of the liver (2-10).
sentences.100: Since the cohort consists of a mixture of socioeconomic status levels, there is probably insignificant confounding due to SES at the plant considered as a whole.
sentences.101: Furthermore, recent infor- mation indicates that these risk gradients may be partially due to smoking patterns (18,19), which would affect epidermoid and small cell undifferentiated lung cancers.
sentences.102: The second objective of this research was to determine whether an excess lung cancer risk of a particular histologic type existed.
sentences.103: The case-comparand study showed that there was an excess of adenocarcinomas and large cell undifferentiated lung cancers among the cases occurring among plant employees compared to other lung cancer cases from the same community.
sentences.104: Because the pathologists reviewed both sets of slides without knowing which were those of plant employees, it is unlikely diagnostic biases occurred.
sentences.105: Histologic specimens were more difficult to find among the cases which died earlier and which were older on the date of death.
sentences.106: However, community comparands were matched with the cases on age and date of diagnosis and had to have specimens available themselves; hence a biased ascertainment by histology between cases and comparands would be unlikely.
sentences.107: The choice of community comparands makes it unlikely that a community wide pollutant was responsible for the excess risk at the plant for types 3 and 4 lung cancer.
sentences.108: Consequently, it can be inferred from Table 3 that the excess lung cancer risk in the cohort was limited to adenocarcinoma and large cell undifferentiated cancer.
sentences.109: Adenocarci- nomas, accounting for a minor proportion of this excess risk, have been shown to be weakly, if at all, related to cigarette smoking (14,(20)(21)(22)
sentences.11: Preliminary re- view of the lung cancer cases indicated they were all adenocarcinomas or large cell undifferentiated tumors-an unusual histologic distribution.
sentences.110: Large cell undifferentiated carcinoma of the lung is the only major histologic type that has appeared to be unrelated to cigarette smoking.
sentences.111: Thus, cigarette smoking was probably not a major confound- ing variable.
sentences.112: However, the role of smoking as a promoter or cocarcinogen cannot be ruled out.
sentences.113: Nev- ertheless, the conclusion of this phase of the inves- tigation was that an excess risk occurred among plant employees for types 3 and 4 lung cancer, especially type 4.
sentences.114: The third objective was to test whether one or more particular chemicals used at the plant were responsible for either the excess risk of all lung cancer or of the types 3 and 4 or just type 4 lung cancer.
sentences.115: The SAED model was specifically devel- oped for this objective.
sentences.116: The major hypothesis was tested for each chemi- cal in the SAED model by using the one-sided t-test of the observed minus expected cumulative doses over all years before death and ten or more years before death (Table 8).
sentences.117: PVC dust was the only chemical that was statistically significant.
sentences.118: These results suggest that an excess of types 3 and 4 lung cancer exists at this plant and is related to PVC dust exposure.
sentences.119: The suggestion of PVC dust being a lung carcin- ogen is biologically plausible.
sentences.12: Although lung tumors have been induced exper- imentally by exposure to VCM (2), the epidemiologic *Industry-wide Studies Branch, Division of Surveillance, Hazard Evaluations and Field Studies, National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, 4676 Columbia Parkway, Cin- cinnati, Ohio 45226.
sentences.120: Almost all PVC parti- cles produced by the emulsion system, one of the systems at this plant, are in the respirable range (23).
sentences.121: These particles could settle in the lungs and conceivably by themselves cause lung cancer.
sentences.122: In fact, one case of supposedly PVC dust-induced pneu- moconiosis has been found in a worker (24), and pulmonary granulomas (25,26) have been induced in animals exposed to PVC dust.
sentences.123: In a large proportional mortality study of 4341 deaths that occurred among PVC fabricators, persons expected to be exposed to VCM and PVC dust demonstrated a slight (PMR = 117) excess lung cancer risk (27).
sentences.124: VCM gas is easily inhaled, and possibly would be in contact with tissue only a short time before being either exhaled or absorbed into the bloodstream.
sentences.125: However, VCM becomes entrapped in the PVC dust and can be released slowly over time.
sentences.126: Thus, PVC dust particles in the lung may slowly release VCM to small adjacent areas of the tissue, prolonging the contact time of that chemical to tissue.
sentences.127: If this latter hypothesis is true, then it begs the question of why almost all of the liver angiosarcoma cases occurred among polymer reactor cleaners who received extremely high VCM doses while the lung cancer cases occurred frequently among the less heavily exposed workers.
sentences.128: In fact, there was no relationship between VCM and lung cancer in this analysis; yet, one would expect the lung to be the major route of entry for VCM regardless of the cancer site.
sentences.13: tDepartment of Community Health, Wellington Clinical School of Medicine, Wellington Hospital, Wellington 2, New Zealand.
sentences.14: tDivision of Chronic Diseases, Center for Environmental Health, Centers for Disease Control, Atlanta, Georgia 30333.
sentences.15: **Department of Epidemiology, School of Public Health, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, North Carolina 27514.
sentences.16: data are suggestive but equivocal.
sentences.17: Two cohort studies found no excess lung cancer risk (4)(5)(6).
sentences.18: In six other studies, elevated lung cancer risks were found overall or among subcohorts; however, few of these excesses were statistically significant due to moderate excess risks and/or small numbers of cases (7)(8)(9)(11)(12)(13).
sentences.19: Because of the uncertainty in the literature regarding the association between VCM exposure and lung cancer and because of the diversity of occupational chemical exposures experienced by the lung cancer cases in our previous study (1), we decided to evaluate our cohort further to determine whether or not lung cancer was associated with VCM or with other chemical exposures.
sentences.2: A standardized mortality ratio of 1.49 for respiratory system cancer (42 observed deaths versus 28.2 expected, p < 0.01) was observed among a cohort of 4806 males employed at a synthetic chemicals plant since its startup in 1942.
sentences.20: Thus, the following research had three objectives: (1) by using a retrospective cohort design, to determine if our previously published excess lung cancer risk among employees exposed to VCM at this synthetic plastics plant also existed for the total plant popula- tion (2) by using a case-comparand study, to de- termine whether an excess lung cancer risk of a particular histologic type was in force at the plant and (3) by using a serially additive expected dose model, to test whether one or more particular chemicals used at the plant were associated with either the excess risk of all or of a specific histologic type of lung cancer.
sentences.21: Methods and Results
sentences.22: Retrospective Cohort Study
sentences.23: The population at risk for the retrospective cohort study consisted of the 4806 males ever employed at this plant from its opening in 1942 until December 31, 1973.
sentences.24: In the absence of individual data on race, everyone was assumed to be white because the company indicated that less than 2% of the population had been nonwhite.
sentences.25: Date of birth and detailed work histories at this plant of all jobs and dates worked by each individual were coded.
sentences.26: By follow-up of all study members from the first date hired at the plant through December 31, 1973, it was determined that 4174 were alive and 559 had died.
sentences.27: The 73 (1.5%) persons lost to follow-up were considered alive throughout the study.
sentences.28: The 16 (3%) deceased persons for whom no death certificates could be located were assumed dead, cause of death unknown.
sentences.29: A modified life table analysis (NIOSH) was used to obtain person years at risk of dying by five year age and calendar time periods.
sentences.3: Upon review of pathologic material, the excess was found to be limited to adenocarcinoma and large cell undifferentiated lung cancer.
sentences.30: United States white male death rates specific for five year age and calendar intervals were used to calculate the expected deaths and standardized mortality ratios (SMR's).
sentences.31: SMR's were tested for statistical significance using the Poisson distribution (onesided).
sentences.32: The cohort was young; by December 31, 1973, only 30% of the cohort, if alive, would have been over 54 years of age.
sentences.33: However, 63% of the cohort had been hired before 1954 and thus had the oppor- tunity to achieve 20 years' latency.
sentences.34: Two separate analyses of the cohort were made.
sentences.35: Initially, all members were considered at risk from their first date of employment at the plant.
sentences.36: This analysis yielded 556 observed and 550 expected deaths (Table 1).
sentences.37: Risk of death due to malignant neoplasms of the central nervous system (SMR = 209) and respiratory system (SMR = 149) were both significantly elevated.
sentences.38: A second "over ten- year latency" analysis was carried out by beginning person-years at risk only after an individual had achieved the tenth anniversary of his first date of employment at the plant.
sentences.39: Results similar to those in the first cohort analysis were found but with slightly higher SMR's.
sentences.4: Many of the workers had been exposed to vinyl chloride, as well as to chlorinated solvents, poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) dust, acrylates and acrylonitrile.
sentences.40: Respiratory system cancer had an SMR of 156 based on 39 observed cases.

sentences.42: Case-Comparand Study
sentences.43: The second objective of this study was to deter- mine whether an excess risk existed for a particular histologic type of lung cancer.
sentences.44: Because no historical data exist on histology-specific lung cancer inci- dence or mortality rates and because histologic classification is somewhat variable between pathologists and over time, a case-comparand design was chosen to accomplish the second objective.
sentences.45: Medical records and pathology reports were obtained on all deceased members of the cohort whose death certificates mentioned cancer or respiratory disease.
sentences.46: For 45 cohort members, primary or un- specified lung cancer was reported on at least one of these three records.
sentences.47: A few persons who died after December 31, 1973, the cohort ending date, were included.
sentences.48: Of the 45 cases, 42 were born in Kentucky or an adjacent state.
sentences.49: Histologic material was re- quested.
sentences.5: To evaluate the association between lung cancer and occupational chemical exposures, detailed work histories for each cohort member were combined with exposure ratings for each of 19 chemicals for each job for each calendar year since 1942.
sentences.50: The worker case group consisted of the 27 of the 45 deceased individuals for whom histologic specimens were available.
sentences.51: As a comparison group, the lung cancer cases (comparands) most closely preceding and succeed- ing the chemical plant worker case in the chronologically ordered hospital pathology logs were selected that matched in age at diagnosis, sex, race, and county of residence.
sentences.52: For four cases, only one matched comparand could be found.
sentences.53: Histologic material was reviewed by a panel of pathologists unaware of the employment histories (case versus comparand status) of the deceased.
sentences.54: The histologic type distributions, according to the Environmental Health Perspectives Veterans' Administration classification scheme (14), were compared between the cases and comparands.
sentences.55: The results of the majority opinion of the pathology panel are listed in Table 2.
sentences.56: The panel found a significantly (p < 0.05, chi-square) higher percentage of large cell undifferentiated (type 4) cancers among the worker cases than among the community comparands (30% vs. 10%).
sentences.57: By using the SMR for respiratory system cancer of 149 in the retrospective cohort study and the observed and expected histologic distribution of lung cancer deaths based on the case-comparand study, Table 3 demonstrates the calculation of histology specific lung cancer SMR's (column C).
sentences.58: If the 27 cases for which histologic specimens were available are considered representative of all 45 lung cancer cases, it appears the excess lung cancer risk appears limited to types 3 and 4, adenocarcinoma and large cell undifferentiated, with the greater risk due to the latter.
sentences.59: Approximately 13.5 of the 14.8 excess lung cancers among the plant workers would be due to adenocarcinoma and large cell undifferentiated carcinoma.
sentences.6: A serially additive expected dose model was then constructed which compared the doses of the chemicals observed for the lung cancer cases to the doses expected based on subcohorts without lung cancer individually matched to the cases.
sentences.60: It appears that there is a histology-specific excess lung cancer risk among workers at this plant and that this differential distribution of cell types is not an artifact of the geographic region nor of the pathologist's techniques.
sentences.61: The fact that this risk occurs for adenocarcinomas and for large cell undifferentiated lung cancers makes it very unlikely that it is due to cigarette smoking.
sentences.62: Serially Additive Expected Dose Model
sentences.63: The third objective was to test whether any presumed occupational chemical exposures were associated with the excess lung cancer risk at the plant.
sentences.64: It was decided to analyze the previously mentioned cohort data in a serially additive ex- pected dose (SAED) model ( 10), obtaining for each lung cancer case the observed and expected doses of each chemical, conditional on certain characteristics.
sentences.65: The purpose of the SAED model is to compare the observed exposure of each case in a study with the exposures of fellow workers close to the case in year of birth, and in age at commencement of work at the company.
sentences.66: If the total work force in the plant under study is referred to as the cohort, then each case can be thought of as belonging to a subcohort of workers with approximately the same year of birth and age at commencement of work in the plant.
sentences.67: In each year that a case worked at the plant, his exposure can be compared with that of the other members of his subcohort who were working in that year.
sentences.68: Company personnel compiled estimated exposures on a scale of 0 to 5 (5 being the highest exposure) for each of 19 chemicals (Table 4).
sentences.69: Each job was as- signed an exposure rank for each calendar year of the study (Table 5).

sentences.84: Discussion
sentences.85: The first objective of this study was to determine if the excess lung cancer risk among employees exposed to VCM also existed for the total plant population, including those persons not exposed to VCM.
sentences.86: The retrospective cohort mortality study showed that respiratory system cancers occurred approximately 50% more frequently among the em- ployees of the entire plant than would have been expected based on age, sex, race, and calendar year specific United States death rates.
sentences.87: A similar excess had been previously shown to exist among the subcohort of employees exposed to VCM (1).

state.hypothesis: Co-exposure to ethanol and vinyl chloride synergistically increases the risk of hepatic angiosarcoma development compared to exposure to vinyl chloride alone.

sentences.0: Effect of Ethanol on Vinyl Chloride Carcinogenesis
sentences.1: Effect of Ethanol on Vinyl Chloride Carcinogenesis
sentences.10: The relationship between inhalation of vinyl chloride (VC) and angiosarcoma of the liver is well documented in man (1,2) and animals (3,4).
sentences.11: Little is known, however, of social or environmental factors which may alter the response of mammals to the chronic inhalation of VC.
sentences.12: Short-term studies suggest that ethanol may modify the potency of the carcinogen VC.
sentences.13: The uptake of VC by rats in vivo was inhibited by prior administration of ethanol (5), and in hepatocyte suspensions of rat liver, 4 mM ethanol inhibited VC metabolism 50% (6).
sentences.14: The following study was designed to elucidate the effects of chronic ethanol ingestion as a cofactor in the carcinogenicity of inhaled VC.
sentences.15: The pathologi- cal responses of rats to ethanol, ethanol with concomitant inhalation of VC, inhalation of VC or ifitered air, were examined in this model system.
sentences.16: Materials and Methods
sentences.17: Three hundred and twenty Sprague-Dawley male rats (Harlan Industries, Indianapolis) were divided into four groups and exposed to toxic agents as indicated in Table 1.
sentences.18: Food and water were withdrawn during VC inhalation and animals were held in compartmented stainless-steel holding-cages which were rotated in the chamber.
sentences.19: Temperature in the 60 ft3 chamber ranged from 70 to 75°F, air flow was 15 ft3/min and humidity -50%.
sentences.2: Four treatment groups (80 male Sprague-Dawley rats/group) were used in a 2 x 2 factorial design: inhalation of 600 ppm vinyl chloride (VC) 4 hr/day, 5 days/week for 1 year; VC and ingestion of 5% ethanol in water (v/v); filtered air and ethanol; filtered air.
sentences.20: The chamber effluent was mixed with natural gas and incinerated at 600-700°C; the incinerator effluent was cooled and scrubbed of HCI with water.
sentences.21: VC (purity 99.9%, Matheson Gas Products) was metered into filtered air prior to entering the chamber.
sentences.22: A Baseline Industries FID 1020 BTR gas chromatograph equipped with a 10 port MPS 1610 multipoint sampler monitored VC concentrations in the chamber and effluent; analysis time, 3 min.
sentences.23: All rats were autopsied, either at the time of spontaneous death, when sacrificed because mori- bund, or at the termination of the study two and one-half years from the first exposure to VC.
sentences.24: Tissues were fixed in neutral formalin, embedded in paraffin and cut at 6 ,um thickness.
sentences.25: Sections were bAdministered 4 weeks prior to VC inhalation, ad libitum, for life.
sentences.26: cOne animal died by accident during experiment.

sentences.3: Ingestion of ethanol was begun 4 weeks prior to inhalation of VC and continued for life or termination of the study at two and one-half years from the first VC exposure.
sentences.30: Results
sentences.31: Timed from the first exposure to VC, average body weights of exposed animals were slowly depressed.
sentences.32: After 18 months the difference between exposed and control rats was about 9%.
sentences.33: There was a more pronounced effect on the survival of exposed animals.
sentences.34: At 18 months, survival was 40% in VC exposed and 18% in VC-ethanol exposed animals in contrast to groups inhaling filtered air in which 70% of the animals ingesting a normal diet and 73% receiving 5% ethanol survived at 18 months.
sentences.35: The decreased survival in VC-exposed groups was due to the development of pathological lesions induced by VC or VC-ethanol rather than to nonspecific causes such as murine pneumonia.
sentences.36: Angiosarcomas and hepatocellular carcinomas were seen in the liver of rats inhaling VC (Table 2).
sentences.37: In some cases, more than one angiosarcoma or carci- noma developed in an animal; the incidence re- ported in Table 2 represents the type of lesion per rat rather than the total number of liver lesions.
sentences.38: The first deaths from angiosarcoma occurred in a VC-ethanol animal at 9 months and at 12 months in a rat exposed to VC alone.
sentences.39: The incidence of angiosarcoma of the liver was increased from 23% (VC alone) to 50% in VC-ethanol exposed rats.
sentences.4: In this model system, ethanol potentiated the carcinogenic response to VC in the liver and produced an excess of neoplasms in animals receiving ethanol alone.
sentences.40: Ethanol had a similar effect on the induction of hepatocellular carcinoma by VC; 44% developed the neoplasm from VC inhalation, and 60% developed the carcinoma from treatment with both agents.
sentences.41: Angiosarcoma of the liver was not found in either filtered air group; however, hepatocellular carcinoma was observed in 10% of the ethanol-ingesting and in 1% of untreated animals.
sentences.42: The incidence of "hyperplastic nodules" is included as an indicator of toxicity.
sentences.43: Endocrine tumors, which comprised the second largest group of neoplasms, are summarized in Table 3.
sentences.44: Malignant tumors included seminomas in the ethanol group, a thyroid tumor in the VC- ethanol group and adrenal tumors in the ethanol and VC-ethanol groups.
sentences.45: The incidence of pituitary adenomas in untreated animals suggests that these rats were unusually susceptible to this lesion.
sentences.46: It appeared that VC had no influence on the development of pancreatic adenomas which consisted mostly of beta cells.
sentences.47: The total number of endocrine tumors in each group indicates a strong effect of ethanol on the endocrine system.
sentences.48: The number of neoplasms occurring at other sites was small in comparison to those that developed in liver and endocrine tissues (Table 4).
sentences.49: Lymphosarcomas were more frequent in VC-ethanol treated rats although these tumors were found in all four groups.

sentences.67: Discussion
sentences.68: In this animal model, ingested ethanol is a cocarcinogen in relation to VC induction of tumors in the liver.
sentences.69: The incidence of angiosarcoma in VC-ethanol dosed rats (50%) was more than double that resulting from VC exposure alone (23%).
sentences.7: Ethanol with or without VC had a strong tumorigenic effect on the endocrine system.
sentences.70: VC-ethanol also induced a greater number of hepatocellular carcinomas (60%) than occurred in VC-treated animals (44%).
sentences.71: The first deaths from angiosarcoma and carcinoma of the liver occurred earlier in VC-ethanol dosed animals indicating a shortened latent period.
sentences.72: The Sprague-Dawley rats used by Maltoni and Lefemine in 1974 (4) were more resistant to the effects of VC on the liver than the animals used in this VC-ethanol study.
sentences.73: Following a year-long exposure to 500 ppm VC 4 hr/day, 5 days/week and observation from first VC exposure for 135 weeks, only 7 of 59 rats (12%) were reported to have angiosarcoma in the liver (4).
sentences.74: Angiosarcomas de- veloped in other sites such as in subcutaneous tissue, the abdominal cavity, neck, lung and uterus.
sentences.75: Hepatocellular carcinomas were not reported.
sentences.76: Zymbal gland carcinomas were seen in 8% of Maltoni's VC exposed animals; none were seen in this study.
sentences.77: Ethanol has been reported to potentiate the toxicity of other halogenated hydrocarbons.
sentences.78: In whole animals, a variety of alcohols increased the hepatotoxicity of carbon tetrachloride (CC14) when ingested 16 to 18 hr prior to inhalation of CC14 (7).
sentences.79: Following acute exposures, CC14 toxicity was en- hanced by ethanol as judged by the elevation of serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase levels.
sentences.8: These results indicate that ethanol is a cocarcinogen in relation to the carcinogen VC.
sentences.80: In similar studies, trichloroethylene (TCE) or 1,1,1- trichloroethane hepatotoxicity was potentiated by ethanol, but only at high concentrations of inhaled TCE or 1,1,1-trichloroethane (8).
sentences.81: Ethanol potentiation of VC carcinogenesis in the liver is probably due to an effect on VC metabolism.
sentences.82: Inhibition of VC uptake (5) and metabolism (6) by ethanol suggests there is a shared step in the oxidation of the two toxic agents.
sentences.83: The most likely candidates for competition are acetaldehyde and chloroacetaldehyde.
sentences.84: The normal substrate, acetal- dehyde, would be oxidized preferentially resulting in an increased half-life of chloroacetaldehyde.
sentences.85: Toxic manifestations of exposures were found which were not related to the neoplastic response.
sentences.86: Many animals died because of neoplasms or second- ary changes caused by tumors; however, death directly attributable to toxicity was not seen.
sentences.87: The toxicity of ethanol will be discussed in another publication.
