sentences.222: Although the statistical power of this study was substantially increased with the use of repeated-measures, the sample size may not have been sufficient to compensate for the narrow variability of the plasma IL.
sentences.223: Interestingly, none of the interaction terms between follow-up time and inflammatory markers examined in this study reached statistical significance.
sentences.224: These null-findings are consistent with the hypothesis that immune response does not alter the rate of telomeric decay.
sentences.225: However, caution should be taken when interpreting these findings, because the limited sample size and follow-up duration of this study precludes definitive evaluation of effect modification of rates.
sentences.226: Although repeated-measures increase the power to detect subtle effects, there was a possibility that the null interactions may be non-informative.
sentences.227: Furthermore, previous studies have shown that the rate of telomeric decay is greatest during early developmental stages of rapid growth between 0–10 years of age; whereas the rate of attrition significantly decreases into post-adolescence and adulthood.
sentences.228: Indeed, only miniscule rates of attrition were observed over a 2 year period in the current study of adults.
sentences.229: Therefore, incredibly substantial effects would be required in a short follow-up period to drive a truly significant interaction term, which would be difficult even in studies with large sample sizes with long follow-up duration.
sentences.23: Erosion of telomeres below critical lengths may lead to aberrant recombination, chromosomal fusion, and even subsequent neoplasia.
sentences.230: The most prominent strength of this study was its prospective design which allowed for improved assessment of the temporality between exposure, outcome, and covariates.
sentences.231: Longitudinal analysis using mixed effects models allows for the incorporations of time-varying exposures, outcomes, and covariates; which permits exploration of the rates of change.
sentences.232: Moreover, the longitudinal design enhances analytical control of confounding.
sentences.233: Additionally, the study design imparts robustness against recall bias of the exposure and differential misclassification; as both the exposure and outcome were independent laboratory measurements.
sentences.234: Moreover, the use of multiple repeated-measures throughout the follow-up period substantially increased the statistical power to detect subtle effects, beyond the apparent sample size of the study.
sentences.235: Notably, exposure assessment was accomplished using highly sensitive electro-chemiluminescent assays on an extensive panel of eleven inflammatory markers.
sentences.236: The Meso Scale Discovery platform offers superior dynamic detection ranges, accuracy, and reproducibility compared to traditional ELISA, which allows for more nuanced analyses of the relationship between inflammatory biomarkers and telomere length.
sentences.237: Furthermore, the outcome was assessed using qPCR which is currently the most labor- and cost-effective methods to measure telomere length in epidemiological studies.
sentences.238: Not only does qPCR correlate well with gold-standard Southern blots, but also requires only a fraction of the genomic DNA, and is robust against detection of centromeric sequences.
sentences.239: As with all scientific investigations, there were limitations of note.
sentences.24: Indeed, numerous epidemiological investigations have implicated diminished telomere length with increased risk of adverse health outcomes.
sentences.240: The practical restrictions of occupational epidemiology studies involving real human subjects creates complexities in the study design and analysis, which requires nuanced appreciation to evaluate.
sentences.241: For instance, union policies and seasonal work-training schedules of the boilermaker subjects created a situation in which entry and exit from the study was staggered, therefore data was unbalanced.
sentences.242: Fortunately, analysis of longitudinal data using versatile linear mixed models does not require balanced data under the aforementioned assumptions.
sentences.243: There may be the possibility of bias due to unmeasured confounders.
sentences.244: However, most notable confounders related to inflammatory markers and telomere length from prior studies were controlled for in the analysis.
sentences.245: Although controlling for time-varying confounders in traditional models may result in selection bias, the degree of bias would depend on the true state-of-affairs between all the related variables; which is inherently unknowable.
sentences.246: As with most occupational cohorts, the sample size of this study was limited.
sentences.247: However, the entire source population from which the subjects were recruited was only 400 union members; therefore our current study population contains a significant proportion of the entirety.
sentences.248: The use of multiple repeated-measures should compensate for this limitation by significantly increasing the statistical power to detect small effect sizes.
sentences.249: There was also the possibility of healthy worker bias (selection bias) in which healthier subjects with lower inflammation, and longer telomeres tended to be recruited and/or remain in the study compared to others.
sentences.25: For instance, previous studies have reported that shorter telomeres were significantly associated with increased overall cancer risk, in addition to decreased survival rate amongst diagnosed cases.
sentences.250: Healthy worker recruitment bias would reduce generalizability of the results to the source population.
sentences.251: Healthy worker selection bias, a form of loss of follow-up, would likely bias the estimates towards the null and underestimate the true effect.
sentences.252: Lastly, the linear mixed models may have been over-adjusted because numerous covariates and white blood cell differentials needed to be controlled in order to minimize bias in the estimates.
sentences.253: Although the variance may have been inflated from over-fitting, statistically significant estimates were still obtained for the analysis involving vascular injury markers and telomere length.
sentences.254: In summary, this study provides an enticing glimpse into the relationship between systemic inflammation, immune response, and genomic degeneration.
sentences.255: Significant negative correlations were found between telomere length and plasma concentrations of CRP and SAA.
sentences.256: Furthermore, marginal yet insignificant negative associations were found between telomere length, and sICAM-1 and sVCAM-1.
sentences.257: Conversely, no significant associations were found between plasma IL concentrations and telomere length.
sentences.258: However, the limited concentration range of some of the IL in this study does not preclude their biological effects on telomere dynamics.
sentences.259: Taken together, the findings from this study suggest that increased systemic inflammation, consistent with vascular injury, is associated with decreased leukocyte telomere length.
sentences.26: Furthermore, truncated telomeres have been found to be associated with increased risk of cardiovascular diseases.
sentences.260: Future prospective studies would benefit from larger sample sizes with a balanced study design in order to discern subtle effects.
sentences.261: Additionally, extended follow-up periods with equally spaced repeated measures would be beneficial in accurately assessing effect modification by inflammatory status on the rate of telomere attrition.
sentences.27: Telomeres truncate by 30–200 bp with every mitotic division as a consequence of intrinsic limitations in lagging-strand DNA synthesis.
sentences.28: As a result, telomere length may provide a portrait of the mitotic history of a cell.
sentences.29: Maintaining sufficient telomere length involves an interplay between factors which erode telomeres, and factors which extend them.
sentences.3: In states of inflammation, subsequent increases in oxidative stress and cellular division may lead to the accelerated erosion of telomeres, crucial genomic structures which protect chromosomes from decay.
sentences.30: Extension of telomeres can be accomplished via activity of the ribonucleoprotein telomerase.
sentences.31: Although constitutively expressed in germ line tissue and omnipotent stem cells, telomerase is only basally expressed in most somatic tissue; thus resulting in gradual decay of telomeric repeats.
sentences.32: Aside from cellular division, telomeric shortening can be further intensified by extrinsic environmental factors which induce oxidative stress under conditions of inflammation.
sentences.33: Therefore, telomere length may also be viewed as a marker that is reflective of cellular coping; providing resilience against biochemically-induced genomic trauma.
sentences.34: Inflammation is a complex physiological response to deleterious stimuli such as injury and infection.
sentences.35: The inflammatory process may be acute as a result of transient stimuli, or may persist as a chronic state as a result of continual exposure.
sentences.36: Chronic inflammation is an underlying pathophysiological basis of numerous diseases such as cancer, myocardial infarction, and lung failure.
sentences.37: With recurrent injury to tissue, subsequent cell death, scarring, and fibrosis may lead to permanent loss of function.
sentences.38: Chronic inflammation may result in both cellular apoptosis and necrosis; facilitating the release of potent reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as superoxides, hydroxyl radicals, and hydrogen peroxide from mitochondria into the vicinity.
sentences.39: These oxidizing agents can induce genomic trauma such as double-stranded breaks and chemical changes to the telomeric sequences of DNA.
sentences.4: However, the association between plasma inflammatory marker concentrations and telomere length has been inconsistent in previous studies.
sentences.40: Indeed, previous studies found that exposure to airborne particulate matter is associated with increased oxidative damage to the genome, as reflected by urinary concentrations of 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), an oxidized nucleoside of DNA.
sentences.41: Furthermore, oxidative stress has also been shown to produce chemical alterations to purines and pyrimidines of telomeric oligonucleotides in the form of 8-oxoguanine adducts.
sentences.42: Should these chemical alterations occur in vivo, inhibition of the interaction between Telomeric repeat-binding factors (TRF1/TRF2) and telomeric sequences may produce instability of the shelterin loop complex; potentially leading to telomeric erosion, dysregulation of gene expression, chromosomal fusion, and disruption of cellular function.
sentences.43: Recent studies found that prolonged exposure to particulate air pollution increases levels of acute phase proteins and vascular injury related inflammatory mediators including C-Reactive Protein (CRP), serum intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (sICAM-1), and serum vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1); important biomarkers of cancer and cardiovascular disease.
sentences.44: Additionally, inflammation may trigger the release of interleukins (IL); a subset of cytokines which can produce highly variable physiological and immune responses in different cell types.
sentences.45: In particular, Interleukin-1 (IL-1) is a pro-inflammatory cytokine primarily produced by macrophages, that mediates inflammatory diseases by initiating and potentiating inflammatory responses and hematopoiesis.
sentences.46: Interleukin-8 (IL-8) is an equally important cytokine produced by macrophages, which acts as a chemo-attractant for neutrophils during acute inflammatory responses.
sentences.47: Moreover, IL-8 has been shown induce rapid mobilization of hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) and subsequent differentiation into leukocytes.
sentences.48: This attribute of IL-8 may have important implications with respect to telomere erosion since increased mitotic division is required to replenish mobilized HSC.
sentences.49: Although inflammation and immune response may be responsible for both cytokine production and telomeric erosion, a number of interleukins including IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, and IL-10 have been shown to increase telomerase activity in vitro which may maintain telomere length; illustrating the complexity of these molecular interactions.
sentences.5: Objective
sentences.50: Despite numerous studies showing the association between telomere length and various chronic diseases, the intricate causal relationship between these variables has been difficult to unravel.
sentences.51: The association between telomere length and disease may be driven by an unmeasured common cause (confounder), such as underlying chronic inflammation.
sentences.52: Although the association between inflammatory markers and chronic health outcomes such as cardiovascular disease has been firmly established, the relationship between these markers and telomere dynamics is less defined.
sentences.53: IL-6, CRP, and Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF-α) have been found in several studies to be associated with decreased telomere length   .
sentences.54: Although well-powered, most of these studies have been of cross-sectional design.
sentences.55: Investigation into the biological interplay between these molecular markers over time in a longitudinal setting would further add to the understanding of the etiological basis of chronic diseases.
sentences.56: Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the longitudinal associations between telomere length and plasma inflammatory biomarker concentrations including: CRP, Serum Amyloid A (SAA), sICAM-1, sVCAM-1, Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF), TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10.
sentences.57: Furthermore, we explored whether these inflammatory biomarkers modify the rate of telomeric change over a 2 year follow-up period.
sentences.58: We hypothesize that increased levels of pro-inflammatory biomarkers is correlated with decreased telomere length, and intensifies the rate of erosion over the follow-up period.
sentences.59: The prospective determination of plasma inflammatory mediators and telomere length at multiple time points is particularly important in addressing numerous gaps in current knowledge, including the dynamic relationship between inflammation, immune response, and genomic trauma.
sentences.6: The purpose of this study was to determine the longitudinal association between telomere length and plasma inflammatory biomarker concentrations including: CRP, SAA, sICAM-1, sVCAM-1, VEGF, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10.
sentences.60: Materials and Methods
sentences.61: Study Design
sentences.62: The Harvard Boilermakers Longitudinal Study is a prospective open-cohort comprised of a series of periodic short-term panel studies.
sentences.63: The source population consists of members of the International Brotherhood of Boilermakers Union, Local 29 in Quincy, MA.
sentences.64: There are currently 400 active union members, 190 of which have been prospectively followed since 1999.
sentences.65: Their primary occupational activity is welding, assembling, and repairing boilers that provide high-pressure steam to drive electrical turbines in power plants.
sentences.66: Therefore, they are exposed to environments with high-levels of occupational fine particulate matter (PM2.5).
sentences.67: The follow-up period for the current longitudinal study was from January 29th 2010 to June 16th 2012.
sentences.68: The current study population consisted of a panel of 87 subjects at baseline.
sentences.69: The inclusion criteria for this study were being male union members, apprentices or journeymen, and over 18 years of age at the time of recruitment.
sentences.7: Methods
sentences.70: The timescale of interest was days of follow-up, while repeated measures of the outcome and predictors were obtained at irregularly spaced time intervals between baseline blood draw and the end of follow-up (Figure 1).
sentences.71: A total of 350 inflammatory biomarker measurements and 244 telomere measurements were obtained for the 87 subjects, with an average of 3 measurements per subject.
sentences.72: One subject diagnosed with arthritis and having a history of myocardial infarction was excluded from the analysis.
sentences.73: Ethics Statement
sentences.74: This observational study was approved the by Institutional Review Board at the Harvard School of Public Health (OHRA Protocol #: P10444, Cardiopulmonary Response to Particulate Exposure, PI: David C. Christiani).
sentences.75: Informed written consent was obtained from all subjects prior to inclusion in the study.
sentences.76: Exposure Assessment
sentences.77: Vascular Injury Biomarkers and Pro-inflammatory Cytokines
sentences.78: Whole blood samples were drawn from subjects by a certified phlebotomist into collection tubes containing EDTA.
sentences.79: Plasma was isolated from whole blood by centrifugation at 1200 RPM for 12 minutes.
sentences.8: The longitudinal study population consisted of 87 subjects.
sentences.80: Plasma samples were then aliquoted into cryogenic tubes and stored at −80°C.
sentences.81: The number of freeze-thaw cycles prior to the assay was limited to one.
sentences.82: Plasma concentrations of CRP, SAA, sICAM-1, and sVCAM-1 were assessed via multiplex electrochemiluminescence using the MULTI-SPOT® 96-well Human Vascular Injury Panel II assay (Meso Scale Discovery, Rockville MD) as per manufacturer's protocol.
sentences.83: Similarly, plasma concentrations of IL-1β, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α, and VEGF were assessed using the 7-plex MULTI-ARRAY® 96-well custom cytokine/chemokine assay.
sentences.84: Duplicate reactions were performed on the same 96-well plate, each using 10 µL of plasma.
sentences.85: Repeated measurements over time for each individual subject were performed on the same 96-well plate.
sentences.86: MULTI-SPOT® vascular injury plates contained an 8-point standard curve from 0–1000 ng/mL with 7-fold dilutions, in order to derive inflammatory marker concentration.
sentences.87: The MULTI-ARRAY® cytokine plates contained an 8-point standard curve from 0–2500 pg/mL with 4-fold dilutions.
sentences.88: Electrochemiluminescent signals from the MULTI-SPOT® and MULTI-ARRAY® assay plates were read using a SI2400A Sector Imager (Meso Scale Discovery, Rockville MD).
sentences.89: Three quality control samples were interspersed through-out all assay plates in duplicate.
sentences.9: The follow-up period was approximately 2 years.
sentences.90: The average within-plate % coefficients of variation (%CVs) ranged from 7.6%–10.9% for the different assays.
sentences.91: The average between-plate %CVs ranged from 12.3%–17.4% for the different assays.
sentences.92: Outcome Assessment
sentences.93: Telomere Real-Time Quantitative PCR
sentences.94: Buffy coat was extracted from whole blood and stored in cell lyses solution at −20°C until DNA extraction.
sentences.95: Peripheral blood leukocyte DNA was extracted using the QIAmp DNA blood kits (QIAGEN, Venlo, Netherlands).
sentences.96: Average relative telomere length was assessed using Real-Time Quantitative PCR (qPCR).
sentences.97: This assay determines the copy-number ratio between telomeric repeats and a single-copy (36B4) reference gene (T/S Ratio, -dCt).
sentences.98: The T/S ratio is reflective of the average telomere length across all chromosomes in a population of cells and was calculated for each participant by subtracting the average 36B4 threshold cycle (Ct) value from the average telomere Ct value.
sentences.99: The T/S ratio value for all experimental samples was then compared to the T/S ratio of a reference sample, consisting of a pooled genomic DNA sample.

state.hypothesis: The presence of dibromoacetonitrile in chlorinated or brominated swimming pools may result in human exposure via skin contact or inhalation.

sentences.0: Background
sentences.1: Swimming pool disinfectants and disinfection by-products (DBPs) have been linked to human health effects, including asthma and bladder cancer, but no studies have provided a comprehensive identification of DBPs in the water and related that to mutagenicity.
sentences.10: Bromoform levels were greater in brominated than in chlorinated pool waters, but we also identified many brominated DBPs in the chlorinated waters.
sentences.100: This information suggested a tentative structural identification of bromochlorobutenedioic acid dimethyl ester, with a monoisotopic molecular mass of 256 Da.
sentences.101: Exact mass data provided by high-resolution MS supported this empirical formula (C6H6O4ClBr).
sentences.102: The observed exact mass of the stronger molecular ion isotopic peak (m/z 257.9116) was within 0.0002 Da of the theoretical mass (m/z 257.9118).
sentences.103: This supported the general structure of bromochlorobutenedioic acid dimethyl ester; however, the exact isomer assignments could not be made by MS data alone because the spectra were too similar, which is often the case for isomers.
sentences.104: Two structural isomers are possible for this empirical formula, (Z) and (E), representing cis and trans isomers, respectively (Figure 1A).
sentences.105: Fortunately, we observed both compounds in most of the pool water concentrates, so it just remained to be determined which specific isomer represented each GC/MS chromatographic peak.
sentences.106: To make this determination, we synthesized the two possible isomers [see Supplemental Material (doi:10.1289/ehp.1001965)] and confirmed by a match of the GC retention time and mass spectra that the (Z) isomer is the first peak at 16.8 min and the (E) isomer is the second peak at 16.9 min in the pool water extracts (Figure 1A).
sentences.107: Mutagenicity
sentences.108: Table 3 and Figure 2 show the mutagenicity data for two samples from the chlorinated pool and two from the brominated pool in strain TA100.
sentences.109: All of the samples were mutagenic in strain TA100 except for sample C5, which was the only sample that showed toxicity—based on a reduction of rev/plate in TA100 at the highest doses (0.04 and 0.05 L-eq/plate).
sentences.11: The pool waters were mutagenic at levels similar to that of drinking water (~ 1,200 revertants/L-equivalents in strain TA100–S9 mix).
sentences.110: Table 4 shows the slopes, r2 values, and standard errors of the slopes for these data; the average mutagenic potency of the three mutagenic samples was 1,190 rev/L-eq.
sentences.111: Only sample B1 was significantly more mutagenic in the GSTT1-expressing strain relative to the nonexpressing strain (Tables 3 and 4).
sentences.112: This indicates that some portion of the mutagenic activity of sample B1 in strain RSJ100 was due to the presence of DBPs that were activated by GSTT1, such as the brominated THMs.
sentences.113: Discussion
sentences.114: Most analytical studies of pool water have measured only a few targeted DBPs, primarily chloroform and other THMs.
sentences.115: Consequently, this study expands considerably our knowledge of the chemical composition and mutagenicity of swimming pool water beyond the chemical analysis of two outdoor pools by and the studies on pool water mutagenicity and genotoxicity.
sentences.116: We found a greater number of DBPs in the chlorinated and brominated indoor pools studied here than have been found in chlorinated outdoor pools, which was not surprising, considering that DBPs can be volatilized or photolyzed in outdoor settings.
sentences.117: In addition, although most people assume that chlorine levels in swimming pools are much higher than in chlorinated drinking water, the mean level of free chlorine (1.28 and 0.50 mg/L in the chlorinated and brominated pools, respectively) was similar to that found typically in drinking water.
sentences.118: Because little is known regarding the mutagenicity and DBP composition of swimming pool water, we compared our data with those for drinking water, which are much more extensive.
sentences.119: In addition, the pool water composition and mutagenicity reported here can be used to better understand the reported health effects of swimming pool water, such as asthma, irritation of eyes/throat/skin, and bladder cancer.
sentences.12: Conclusions
sentences.120: Nitrogen-containing DBPs
sentences.121: In general, we observed more nitrogen-containing DBPs (N-DBPs) in these pool water samples than are found typically in chlorinated drinking water.
sentences.122: For example, we found a greater number of haloamides, halonitriles, haloanilines, haloanisoles, and halonitro-compounds than typically found in drinking water, and several chemicals within these families have not been reported previously in drinking water.
sentences.123: In addition, we detected mono- and dichloramine in the pool waters (means of 0.29 and 0.38 mg/L, respectively, for mono- and dichloramine in the chlorinated pool, and a mean of 0.27 mg/L for monochloramine in the brominated pool).
sentences.124: Because DPD analysis of chloramines cannot differentiate organic from inorganic forms of these compounds, it is possible that these levels are overestimated by the occurrence of organic chloramines in the swimming pool waters.
sentences.125: Model studies with batch experiments show that survival of chloramines depends on the chlorine:nitrogen ratio.
sentences.126: Considering this, the low concentrations of mono- and dichloramine reported in Table 1 are consistent with chlorine oxidation of continuous supplies of small amounts of nitrogen compounds coming from urine, sweat, skin, and other human residues.
sentences.127: These levels are also similar to those reported by other researchers who used membrane-introduction MS, which does not have issues with interferences from organic chloramines.
sentences.128: The N-DBPs, including chloramines, were not surprising to find because pool waters have a greater contribution of nitrogen-containing precursors due to human inputs.
sentences.129: Because chloramines are known to cause eye irritation and other problems, pool operators generally try to add enough chlorine to get beyond the “break point,” such that these chloramines are destroyed, leaving residual chlorine.
sentences.13: This study identified many new DBPs not identified previously in swimming pool or drinking water and found that swimming pool waters are as mutagenic as typical drinking waters.
sentences.130: However, the amount of chlorine needed to reach “break point” is also dependent on other amines in the water.
sentences.131: As we observed in this study, this goal is not always achieved because of continuous human inputs and rapid reactions forming chloramines.
sentences.132: A few other N-DBPs also have been reported in swimming pool waters, including organic chloramines, and nitrosamines, several of which are carcinogenic.
sentences.133: Comparison of brominated versus chlorinated pool waters
sentences.134: Bromoform levels were much higher in the pools treated with bromine versus chlorine, but interestingly, other DBPs and their levels were similar in brominated versus chlorinated pools, likely owing to the high levels of bromide present already in Barcelona source waters that feed into drinking water treatment and further swimming pool treatment.
sentences.135: In addition, when THMs are compared on a molar basis, the chlorinated pool actually contained somewhat higher levels of total THMs (mean, 306 nM) than the brominated pool (mean, 242 nM); this was possibly due to the carbon filtration used at the brominated pool that was not used at the chlorinated pool.
sentences.136: Mutagenicity
sentences.137: In the only other mutagenicity study of swimming pool water, found that three public indoor pools in Victoria, British Columbia (Canada), produced approximately 20,000 rev/L-eq in Salmonella TA100 (without S9 mix), compared with our finding of an average of 1,190 rev/L-eq in the two indoor pools in Barcelona.
sentences.138: However, their solvent-extraction method was considerably different from ours, involving ether and acetone, whereas we used ethyl acetate.
sentences.139: Although a direct comparison of the data is not possible, our study confirms their pioneering work from three decades ago showing that swimming pool water is mutagenic.
sentences.14: Disinfection by-products (DBPs) represent a ubiquitous exposure in developed countries.
sentences.140: In general, extracts of drinking water induce an average of 1,100 rev/L-eq in Salmonella strain TA100 (without S9 mix); however, values as high as approximately 15,000 rev/L-eq have been reported.
sentences.141: Concentration methods such as reverse osmosis recover levels of mutagenic activity lower than those recovered by XAD resin, which is why we used XAD to prepare extracts of pool water.
sentences.142: Our finding that the pool water mutagenicity was similar to that of drinking water may reflect the fact that the levels of mutagenic DBPs in the pool waters were similar to those in drinking water, despite the differences in the levels of specific classes of DBPs described above in pool versus drinking water.
sentences.143: Our finding that some of the mutagenic activity of one sample (B1) from the brominated pool water was due to activation by GSTT1 suggests the presence of compounds that are activated to mutagens by this enzyme, such as brominated THMs, some methylene dihalides and bifunctional butanes, and/or 1,1-dichloropropene.
sentences.144: Our chemical analysis (Table 1) showed that sample B1 had high concentrations of brominated THMs, especially bromoform.
sentences.145: The high cytotoxicity and lack of mutagenicity of sample C5 may reflect the fact that the concentration of chloroform was 30% higher in this sample than in sample C4.
sentences.146: Perhaps the higher concentration of chloroform, which is cytotoxic but not mutagenic, produced the observed cytotoxicity, preventing detection of mutagenic activity of the other DBPs present in sample C5.
sentences.147: As reviewed by, many other DBPs in drinking water that we have now identified in pool waters are known to be mutagenic and/or carcinogenic, including the haloacetic acids, halonitromethanes, haloamides, haloacetonitriles, and unregulated haloacids.
sentences.148: In addition to the mix of mutagenic DBPs identified in the pool water, many other DBPs have not yet been studied for health effects, and no doubt, many other DBPs remain to be identified that also may contribute to the observed mutagenicity of swimming pool water.
sentences.149: In this regard, the study by, which found that the low-molecular-weight fraction of extracts from indoor and outdoor pools in Germany was the most potent of all fractions for inducing DNA damage in mammalian cells (using the comet assay), suggests that the low-molecular-weight DBPs may be most responsible for the genotoxic effect of swimming pool water.
sentences.15: DBPs are formed by the reaction of disinfectants (e.g., chlorine, chloramines, ozone, or chlorine dioxide) with natural organic matter and/or bromide/iodide, and they are an unintended consequence of trying to kill pathogens in drinking water and swimming pools.
sentences.150: Also using the comet assay, found that pool water was more genotoxic than the source tap water; a similar analysis using the Ames assay would help in characterizing the relative mutagenicity of drinking versus pool water.
sentences.151: Sources of mutagens unique to pool water could include active agents in sunscreens, which can be transformed to mutagens by exposure to free chlorine under conditions similar to swimming pool water.
sentences.152: Our limited data indicate that the mutagenic potencies of chlorinated versus brominated pool waters were similar, as were the dose ranges over which the pool waters were mutagenic, approximately 0.1–0.3 L-eq/plate (Figure 2).
sentences.153: In contrast, the typical dose range for drinking water mutagenicity is 0.3–1.5 L-eq/plate.
sentences.154: This difference reflects the considerably higher toxicity of swimming pool water relative to drinking water, with the highest testable mutagenic dose of pool water being the lowest mutagenic dose of drinking water.
sentences.155: Conclusions
sentences.156: We identified > 100 DBPs in two indoor pools, including a prevalence of N-DBPs, likely formed from nitrogen-containing precursors from human inputs.
sentences.157: This study provides the most comprehensive analysis to date of DBPs in swimming pool waters, as well as a clear demonstration of their mutagenicity.
sentences.158: In addition, many DBPs we identified are new and have not been reported previously in pool waters.
sentences.159: Bromoform levels were much greater in the brominated versus chlorinated pools.
sentences.16: More than 600 DBPs have been identified in drinking water, and many of them are mutagenic or carcinogenic.
sentences.160: Compared with previous research on outdoor pools, we found a much greater number of DBPs in these indoor pools.
sentences.161: The mutagenicity of these pool waters was similar to that of drinking water, indicating that the levels of mutagenic DBPs are similar in both waters.
sentences.162: Subjects who swam in the mutagenic, chlorinated pool water evaluated in this study had increases in genotoxicity biomarkers that were associated with the concentrations of brominated THMs, but not chloroform, in their exhaled breath.
sentences.163: These findings are especially relevant with regard to a case–control study by in this issue that identifies an enhanced risk for bladder cancer associated with DBP exposure among people with genotypes that metabolize various DBPs.
sentences.164: Further research on a wide array of swimming pools under various conditions of maintenance and use are warranted based on the limited but developing data now available on the chemical composition and health risks of swimming pool water.
sentences.17: This complex mixture of DBPs includes volatile and skin-permeable DBPs, such as trihalomethanes (THMs) and haloketones (:).
sentences.18: Inhalation and dermal absorption, which are the primary routes of exposure to DBPs during swimming, leads to higher blood levels of THMs than do oral exposures.
sentences.19: Swimming pools constitute environments with high levels of DBPs in water and air due to continuous disinfection and constant organic load from bathers (e.g., urine, sweat, cosmetics, skin cells, and hair).
sentences.2: Objectives
sentences.20: One of the most prevalent DBPs in chlorinated swimming pools is THMs, with average concentrations ranging from 16 μg/L to 132 μg/L.
sentences.21: Given the high nitrogen content of organic matter from bathers, nitrogenated species such as haloacetonitriles, nitrosamines, and chloramines are found in swimming pool water.
sentences.22: Chronic exposure to DBPs through different routes has been associated with an increased risk for bladder cancer.
sentences.23: Trichloramine and other volatile chemicals in swimming pools are respiratory irritants; pool attendance has been associated with asthma and other respiratory effects in Olympic swimmers and pool workers, and less clearly with recreational adult swimmers and children.
sentences.24: However, the mechanisms are poorly understood, and it is not known with certainty whether trichloramine or other volatile pool DBPs are responsible.
sentences.25: Despite the public health relevance, only a few studies, most rather recent, have investigated the chemistry and potential health effects of swimming pool water.
sentences.26: A complete chemical characterization of DBPs in indoor swimming pools has not been reported.
sentences.27: The only mutagenicity study of swimming pool water reported that organic extracts from three public indoor pools in Victoria, British Columbia (Canada), were mutagenic in Salmonella TA100.
sentences.28: The authors found that acidified extracts eluted with ether were more mutagenic in the presence of metabolic activation (rat liver S9) than without S9; however, nonacidified extracts eluted with acetone were mutagenic only in the absence of S9.
sentences.29: One genotoxicity study of swimming pool water reported that the water and its fractions induced DNA damage in Hep-G2 cells (comet assay) and that most of the genotoxicity was in the lower-molecular-weight DBP fraction.
sentences.3: We performed a comprehensive identification of DBPs and disinfectant species in waters from public swimming pools in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain, that disinfect with either chlorine or bromine and we determined the mutagenicity of the waters to compare with the analytical results.
sentences.30: Another study using the comet assay showed that pool water was more genotoxic than the source tap water and that the type of disinfectant and illumination conditions altered the genotoxicity.
sentences.31: The present study involves an investigation in Barcelona, Spain, where we examined 49 healthy nonsmoking volunteers before and after swimming in public swimming pools treated with either chlorine or bromine to evaluate personal exposure and a range of biomarkers of genotoxicity and respiratory damage.
sentences.32: To complement the exposure assessment, we evaluated the mutagenicity of the pool waters in the Salmonella mutagenicity assay and screened for DBPs, comprehensively identifying most DBPs detected and quantifying a few targeted DBPs and disinfectant species (THMs, chlorine, monochloramine, dichloramine, and trichloramine) in the pool waters and in the air phase above the water (THMs and trichloramine).
sentences.33: In this article we present a comprehensive identification of DBPs and disinfectant species in the pool waters and compare the species formed in chlorinated versus brominated pool water with the corresponding mutagenicity of the waters.
sentences.34: Materials and Methods
sentences.35: Sampling
sentences.36: Water samples were collected from two large public swimming pools in Barcelona, Spain.
sentences.37: One pool (33 × 25 × 2 m in size) used chlorine (sodium hypochlorite) for disinfection, after sand filtration; the other pool (20.9 × 13.2 × 1.3 m in size) used bromine (1-bromo-3-chloro-5,5-dimethyl-2,4-imidazolidinedione) for disinfection, after sand and granulated carbon filtration.
sentences.38: Floor-to-ceiling height was 10 m and 5 m in the chlorinated and brominated pools, respectively.
sentences.39: Quantitative analyses
sentences.4: Methods
sentences.40: Free chlorine, monochloramine, dichloramine, trichloramine, and THMs were measured in composite pool water samples (1 L) collected from four different locations.
sentences.41: Free chlorine, monochloramine, dichloramine, and trichloramine were measured immediately using the N,N-diethyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPD) method with a portable photometer (DINKO Instruments, Barcelona, Spain).
sentences.42: Water samples (40 mL) for THM measurements were quenched with 5 mg sodium thiosulfate and stored at 4°C until analysis on the same day.
sentences.43: Chloroform, bromodichloromethane, dibromochloromethane, and bromoform were measured using purge-and-trap gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS) (Tekmar 3100, Voyager MS; ThermoFisher, Waltham, MA, USA) following the method described by.
sentences.44: Sixty-eight samples were collected from the chlorinated pool and 12 from the brominated pool for these quantitative analyses.
sentences.45: Indoor air samples to measure THMs were collected with a pump located 60 cm above the floor and 1.5 m from the pool border.
sentences.46: Air was pumped (7 mL/min) for 20 min through a Tenax TA cartridge (1.8 g; Supelco, Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA).
sentences.47: Quality control was assured by daily calibration of the pump.
sentences.48: Chloroform, bromodichloromethane, dibromochloromethane, and bromoform were determined through an automatic thermal desorption unit (ATD 400; Perkin-Elmer, Madrid, Spain) coupled to a GC-electron capture detector (Perkin-Elmer).
sentences.49: Sixty-eight air samples were collected from the chlorinated pool, and 12 from the brominated pool.
sentences.5: We used gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS) to measure trihalomethanes in water, GC with electron capture detection for air, low- and high-resolution GC/MS to comprehensively identify DBPs, photometry to measure disinfectant species (free chlorine, monochloroamine, dichloramine, and trichloramine) in the waters, and an ion chromatography method to measure trichloramine in air.
sentences.50: Trichloramine was measured in pool air samples by pumping air (1.2 L/min) for 115 min, within 1 m from the water and at a height of 60 cm from the floor level, using a method described originally by.
sentences.51: Trichloramine was captured on two 37-mm quartz-fiber filters, one of which was placed as a backup filter, both impregnated with 500 mL of a solution of diarsenic trioxide (4 g/L As2O3), sodium carbonate (40 g/L Na2CO3), and glycerol (40 mL/L C3H8O3).
sentences.52: These filters were placed in a sampling cassette with a 37-mm cellulose support filter and a 37-mm Teflon filter to prevent chloride from airborne water droplets from being captured in the sampler.
sentences.53: Impregnated filters were desorbed in 10-mL ultra-high quality, ultrapure water (specific conductivity, 17.8 MΩ/cm at 25°C), sonicated for 30 min, and centrifuged for 15 min at 3,000 × g after sampling.
sentences.54: Trichloramine was reduced to chloride and subsequently analyzed by ion chromatography (Dionex DX100; Dionex BV, Bavel, the Netherlands; AS14A guard and AS14 highly selective anion column with self-regenerating suppressor; conductivity detector; flow rate, 1.0 mL/min).
sentences.55: Six samples were collected from the chlorinated pool, and three from the brominated pool.
sentences.56: Preparation of water extracts and concentrates
sentences.57: For comprehensive GC/MS analyses and mutagenicity testing, pool water samples were collected at approximately noon on five different sampling events for the chlorinated pool (7 and 24 May, 11 June, and 17 September 2007) and two different sampling events for the brominated pool (16 July and 15 October 2007).
sentences.58: Samples (28 L each) were collected using 2-L Teflon bottles (headspace-free) and were shipped overnight in coolers with icepacks to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency laboratory in Athens, Georgia (USA).
sentences.59: Water samples were extracted immediately upon arrival using the XAD resin process of [for further details, see Supplemental Material (doi:10.1289/ehp.1001965)].
sentences.6: We assessed mutagenicity with the Salmonella mutagenicity assay.
sentences.60: The final extract was divided for comprehensive GC/MS analysis (1.0 mL, equivalent to 20 L water) and mutagenicity analysis (0.4 mL, equivalent to 8 L water, or 20,000×).
sentences.61: Comprehensive GC/MS analyses
sentences.62: Half of the 1.0-mL extract was derivatized with diazomethane [see Supplemental Material (doi:10.1289/ehp.1001965)] to enable the identification of haloacids (through their corresponding methyl esters); the other half was analyzed directly for other DBPs.
sentences.63: Comprehensive GC/MS analyses were performed on a high-resolution magnetic sector mass spectrometer (Autospec; Waters, Inc., Milford, MA, USA) equipped with an Agilent model 6890 gas chromatograph (Agilent, Santa Clara, CA, USA) and operated at an accelerating voltage of 8 kV and source temperature of 200°C, in both low-resolution (1,000) and high-resolution (10,000) modes.
sentences.64: Injections of 1 μL extract were introduced via a split/splitless injector (in splitless mode) onto a GC column (DB-5, 30-m × 0.25-mm i.d. 0.25-μm film thickness; J&W Scientific/Agilent, Santa Clara, CA, USA).
sentences.65: The GC temperature program consisted of an initial temperature of 35°C (4 min) and an increase at 9°C/min to 285°C (held for 30 min).
sentences.66: Transfer lines were held at 280°C, and the injection port at 250°C.
sentences.67: For qualitative identifications, mass spectra of unknown compounds in the finished and raw water concentrates were subjected initially to library database searching (using the 2005 NIST Mass Spectral Library database; National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD).
sentences.68: However, many DBPs were not present in the library database; in those cases, and also where a library match was insufficient to offer a tentative identification, high-resolution MS was used to provide empirical formulas for molecular ions and fragments.
sentences.69: Mass spectra were also interpreted extensively to provide tentative structural identifications.
sentences.7: Results
sentences.70: When possible, pure standards were obtained to confirm identifications through a match of GC retention times and mass spectra.
sentences.71: Chemical standards
sentences.72: Chemical DBP standards were either synthesized (CanSyn Chem. Corp., Toronto, ON, Canada) or purchased at the highest level of purity (Sigma-Aldrich, Milwaukee, WI, USA).
sentences.73: The synthesis of (E)- and (Z)-bromochlorobutenedioic acid is presented in Supplemental Material (doi:10.1289/ehp.1001965).
sentences.74: Mutagenicity assays
sentences.75: The 20,000× XAD/ethyl acetate extracts described above were solvent-exchanged into dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO; Burdick and Jackson, Muskegon, MI, USA) and diluted to 10,000× and 1,000×.
sentences.76: We performed the standard plate-incorporation Salmonella (Ames) mutagenicity assay in the base-substitution strain TA100 (hisG46 rfa ΔuvrB, pKM101), obtained from B.N. Ames, Children’s Hospital Oakland Research Institute (Oakland, CA, USA).
sentences.77: We also tested the extracts in Salmonella strain RSJ100, which expresses the rat GSTT1 gene, and its control strain TPT100.
sentences.78: These strains are homologous to TA100 except that they do not contain the pKM101 plasmid and either do or do not express GSTT1.
sentences.79: These strains were obtained from F.P. Guengerich (Vanderbilt University, Nashville, TN, USA).
sentences.8: We identified > 100 DBPs, including many nitrogen-containing DBPs that were likely formed from nitrogen-containing precursors from human inputs, such as urine, sweat, and skin cells.
sentences.80: We did not use S9 mix because we assumed that pool water was similar to drinking water, and drinking water extracts are most mutagenic in the absence of S9 mix.
sentences.81: Extracts were tested up to 100 μL/plate over a dose range of 0.01–0.3 L-equivalents (L-eq)/plate based on doses used for drinking water and a dose-range–finding study.
sentences.82: Because of limited amounts of samples available for testing in all three bacterial strains, only two samples from the chlorinated pool (C4 and C5) and two from the brominated pool (B1 and B2) were evaluated for mutagenicity, each at one plate per dose in single experiments.
sentences.83: We incubated the plates for 3 days at 37°C, counted the colonies [revertants (rev)] on an automatic colony counter, and calculated linear regressions over the linear portion of the dose–response curves to determine the mutagenic potencies (rev/L-eq).
sentences.84: We defined a positive result as a dose-related response with two or more times the number of revertants observed in the DMSO control.
sentences.85: The positive control for all strains was sodium azide at 3 μg/plate.
sentences.86: We calculated linear regressions, slope values, the standard error of the slopes, and r2 values of the dose–response curves and then compared the regression lines between strains RSJ100 (GST+) and TPT100 (GST−) to obtain p-values using Statgraphics Centurion XVI (Statpoint Technologies, Inc., Warrenton, VA, USA).
sentences.87: The model tests the null hypothesis that the slopes are equal; we set α = 0.05 for the F-test with 2 degrees of freedom.
sentences.88: Results
sentences.89: DBPs
sentences.9: Many DBPs were new and have not been reported previously in either swimming pool or drinking waters.
sentences.90: Table 1 lists levels of free chlorine, chloramines, and THM species in the pool water and air.
sentences.91: Although we did not detect trichloramine in the pool waters, we did find mean levels of 0.29 and 0.08 mg/m3 in the chlorinated and brominated pool air, respectively, indicating that most of it volatilized from the water into the air.
sentences.92: We identified > 100 DBPs comprehensively in the pool waters [Table 2; see also Supplemental Material, Figure S1 (doi:10.1289/ehp.1001965)], including a large number of haloacids, halomethanes, haloacetonitriles, haloaldehydes, haloketones, halonitromethanes, haloamides, haloalcohols, and halophenols.
sentences.93: All of these contained either bromine or chlorine; we detected no iodinated DBPs.
sentences.94: Most DBPs have not been reported previously for swimming pool waters, and many were not present in the mass spectral library database.
sentences.95: The identification of (E)- and (Z)-bromochlorobutenedioic acid (in their corresponding methyl ester forms) illustrates how we identified unknown DBPs.
sentences.96: They eluted at different retention times (Figure 1A) but exhibited similar mass spectra (indicative of isomeric structures), each containing m/z 256/258/260, 225/227/229, and 59 (Figure 1B).
sentences.97: The loss of 31 Da (typically OCH3) at m/z 225 and the presence of m/z 59 [typically C(O)OCH3] suggested the presence of a carboxylic acid methyl ester in the structures, with a molecular ion of m/z 256/258/260.
sentences.98: Further, the m/z 256/258/260 isotopic pattern was indicative of one bromine and one chlorine atom, matching the calculated theoretical pattern [see Supplemental Material, Figure S2 (doi:10.1289/ehp.1001965)].
sentences.99: This pattern results from the overlap of the two natural isotopes of bromine (79Br and 81Br) with the two natural isotopes of chlorine (35Cl and 37Cl).

state.hypothesis: Exposure to high levels of arsenic in drinking water during pregnancy increases the risk of neonatal mortality.

sentences.1: Children's Health Articles Chronic Arsenic Exposure and Risk of Infant Mortality in Two Areas of Chile
sentences.10: The findings from this investigation may support a role for arsenic exposure in increasing the risk of late fetal and infant mortality.
sentences.100: For arsenic as a continuous variable, we used available histori- cal arsenic levels in drinking water supplies to estimate averages for each 4-year period in each location.
sentences.101: For the low exposures in Valparaiso, we assumed arsenic water levels of 5 pg/L.
sentences.102: The dichotomous variable (present/ absent) was created to serve as an exposure indicator only for Antofagasta during the years of high arsenic exposure (1958)(1959)(1960)(1961)(1962)(1963)(1964)(1965)(1966)(1967)(1968)(1969)(1970).
sentences.103: Because arsenic levels decreased after the installation of the arsenic-removal plant in March 1970, we only considered three higharsenic year groups: 1958-1961, 1962-1965,  and 1966-1969.
sentences.104: For all other time periods and locations, this indicator variable was coded as a zero (absent).
sentences.105: City, calendar time, and one of the arsenic exposure variables were included in the Poisson regression models and goodness-of-fit was evaluated using graphical approaches plotting observed and expected rates over calendar time.
sentences.106: We calculated adjusted rate ratios (RRs)
sentences.107: and the associated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) from the parameters estimated by the model.
sentences.108: The calendar time period 1974-1977 served as the referent period for the model, chosen because it was after the end of the high arsenic period and quite close to the mid point of the entire study time.
sentences.109: The analysis was performed using the PROC GENMOD procedure provided in the SAS software (55).
sentences.11: Key words arsenic, Chile, drinking water, infnt mortality, neonatal death, reproductive effect, stillbirth.
sentences.110: The model was fit with the Poisson distribution with the link function as the log and the offset as the log of the appropriate denominator (i.e., total births).
sentences.111: The results obtained using the arsenic expo- sure variable as either a continuous or as a categorical variable were not materially dif- ferent; therefore, the results are shown for arsenic as a categorical variable.
sentences.112: Results
sentences.113: Demographic data for Valparalso and Antofagasta representing several decades were obtained from INE census reports (47-50) and are presented in Table 1.
sentences.114: These data indicate that Antofagasta and Valparaiso are comparable on a number of characteristics, although these indicators have changed over time.
sentences.115: Infant and late fetal mortality rates declined markedly in Chile during the study period of 1950-1996, as illustrated in Figure 2.
sentences.116: This decrease is characteristic of most Latin American countries; it follows the gen- eral trend observed in industrialized nations and is largely due to improvements in living conditions and health care (56).
sentences.117: The rate of decline up to the 1980s was the most pro- nounced for postneonatal mortality, with more gradual declines evident for neonatal and late fetal mortality.
sentences.118: Figures   (53).
sentences.119: calendar period 1958-1961 and declined thereafter.
sentences.12: Environ Health Perspect 108:667-673 (2000).
sentences.120: The increases and declines vary by outcome, but overall they coincide with the period of higher arsenic levels in the drink- ing water supply of Antofagasta.
sentences.121: Table 3 shows the comparison of rates between the two areas.
sentences.122: During the period of maximum difference in rates between the two communities (1958)(1959)(1960)(1961), Antofagasta had an excess rate of approximately 20 late fetal deaths, 24 neonatal deaths, and 24 post- neonatal deaths per 1,000 births (Table 3).
sentences.123: The total estimated excess of 68 deaths per thousand births is equivalent to approximate- ly 770 of the 1,900 combined late fetal and infant deaths which occurred during that time period.
sentences.124: Subsequent to 1974, mortality rates exhibit a more gradual decline and are very similar between the two communities.
sentences.125: Results from the Poisson regression analysis of the rates of late fetal, neonatal, and postneonatal mortality are given in Table 4.
sentences.126: We observed significantly elevated RRs for high arsenic exposure in association with each of the three mortality outcomes, after adjustment for location and calendar time.
sentences.127: The association between arsenic exposure and late fetal mortality exhibited the strongest association (RR = 1.72; CI, 1.54-1.93), with neonatal mortality (RR = 1.53; CI, 1.40-1.66), and postneonatal mortality (RR = 1.26; CI, 1.18-1.34) also yielding elevated RRs, respectively.
sentences.128: The variable for location demonstrated a significant association with each outcome, although the magnitude was less than that between arsenic exposure and each outcome.
sentences.129: The rate ratios for the 4-year calendar groups exhibited the predictable secular declines over time.

sentences.130: Discussion
sentences.131: The results of this study indicate that expo- sure to inorganic arsenic from public water supplies may be associated with an increased risk of infant mortality.
sentences.132: Specifically, the data suggest that arsenic exposure may represent a greater risk for late fetal mortality with a lower, but still elevated, risk for neonatal and postneonatal mortality.
sentences.133: This association was evident after controlling for geographic location and calendar time in Poisson regression models.
sentences.134: The mortality rates in both Antofagasta and Valparaiso reflect the well-established decline in late fetal, neonatal, and postneonatal mortality that occurred in Chile over the study period (57.
sentences.135: Improvement in the standard of living, development of pro- grams for maternal and infant care (prenatal, nutritional supplementation, and health education, among others), and the decrease in birth rate are considered the primary fac- tors accounting for the substantial improve- ment in infant mortality rates during this period (56,58,59).
sentences.136: The steeper decline in postneonatal mortality supports these changing patterns of infant mortality because diar- rheal infections and other childhood diseases that are much less fatal under improved health and living conditions are common throughout the first year of life.
sentences.137: &Mortality rates were calculated per 1,000 live births for neonatal and postneonatal period, and per 1,000 total births (live + late fetal) for the late fetal period.
sentences.138: Although both Antofagasta and Val- paraiso experienced substantial improve- ments in their overall infant mortality rates over the study period, the pattern of infant mortality for these two communities was quite different before the 1970s.
sentences.139: Antofagasta exhibited marked increases in late fetal, neonatal, and postneonatal mortality in 1958-1961.
sentences.14: Arsenic is a naturally occurring element that is present in the environment in both organic and inorganic forms.
sentences.140: As compared to Valparaiso, these rates remained elevated until 1974-1977 for late fetal mortality, and until 1970-1973 for neonatal and postneonatal mortality.
sentences.141: The pattern of increase and subsequent decline in Antofagasta's mortality rates show a close temporal relationship with the rather sudden and sharp rise in the levels of arsenic in the city's public water supply from 1958 until March 1970, when an arsenic-removal facility was installed, and suggest a possible role for inorganic arsenic in the observed increase in infant mortality.
sentences.142: As in the rest of the country, the decline in mortality rates in Antofagasta during the overall study period was likely a result of other nonarsenic-related factors such as improvement in health care and standard of living, which affected all of the regions in Chile.
sentences.143: Moreover, starting in the 1960s, Region II, which includes the city of Anto- fagasta, experienced a surge of economic expansion, with a rate of growth and devel- opment greatly surpassing that of the rest of the country: the increase in adjusted annual per-capita income was greater by far in Region II than any other region (60).
sentences.144: This expansion brought improvements in region- al health care as well, which may explain, at least in part, the fact that in the period before 1958 Antofagasta had higher late fetal and infant mortality rates than Val- paraiso, whereas after 1970 the rates declined to comparable levels between the two towns.
sentences.145: It appears that the increase in arsenic in the water supply served to delay the improvement in fetal and infant health until the arsenic-removal plant was installed (Figures 345).
sentences.146: The results of this study should be considered within the context of limitations in the study design and in the type of data obtained.
sentences.147: In general, ecologic studies are susceptible to biases that pertain to the lack of individual data on exposure, outcomes, and confounders.
sentences.148: These biases, known as the ecologic fallacy, have been discussed in detail elsewhere (61).
sentences.149: In this study, although expo- sure was measured at the group level, public water was consumed by most residents in each of the communities, the water supply came from one main source at each location, and we adjusted for community differences in the model.
sentences.15: Human exposures to the more toxic inorganic arsenic compounds result from exposures in occupational set- tings, such as metal smelting and pesticide production, as well as from medicinal treatments and environmental sources (1,4.
sentences.150: However, we lacked data on individual-level confounders, and therefore we cannot definitely exclude the possibility of an ecologic bias.
sentences.151: Nevertheless, the distinct temporal pattern of infant mortality rates in Antofagasta as compared to Valparaiso argues against this bias.
sentences.152: That is, residual confounding from factors not available would have to closely relate to the timing of the high arsenic exposure documented in Antofagasta.
sentences.153: The change in the arsenic level of the water supply was an indisputable event, and no other environmental pollutant has been described to account for the many documented health effects experienced by the population of Antofagasta during the study time period (8,20,44,46,(62)(63)(64)(65).
sentences.154: Thus, it would not be surprising if these reproductive events were also due to the con- sumption of water with high arsenic.
sentences.155: The underascertainment of both birth and death registrations is typically a poten- tial concern of studies of this design.
sentences.156: With regard to birth registration, there is evidence of underascertainment, which has substantially declined over time.
sentences.157: In Chile, children whose births are not registered by March of the year after they were born are categorized separately.
sentences.158: A study of birth registrations from 1955-1988 showed variations ranging from 11.4 to 4.2% in late birth registrations (66).
sentences.159: We also observed variations between regions; Antofagasta and Valparaiso were consistently among those with the lowest late registration rates.
sentences.16: The use of drinking water with elevated arsenic concentrations, primarily from natural cont- amination, has been the main source of environmental exposures in populations worldwide, including but not limited to communities in Taiwan (3), India (4), Bangladesh (5), Thailand (6), Mexico  (7), Chile (8), Argentina (9), China (10), and Hungary (11).
sentences.160: The increase in births that occur in hospitals (42.3% in 1953 vs.  99.7% in 1994) and births assisted by medical professionals (57.5% in 1953 vs. 100% in 1994) also impacts the completeness of birth registration.
sentences.161: Regional statistics show that Antofagasta and Valparaiso were two of the four provinces with the highest percentage of physician-assisted births in 1953, compared to the rest of Chile (6/).
sentences.162: Death registration is also characterized by omissions, especially for newborns that died in the first hours or days after birth.
sentences.163: A study conducted in Santiago in 1968-1969 showed that over one-half of the hospitalborn babies who died were not registered (68).
sentences.164: Another study in Santiago found that 13% of the deaths of children younger than 5 years of age (69) were not registered, and most of this underregistration occurred for deaths in the neonatal period.
sentences.165: In Chile, the certification of infant deaths by a physician increased from 55% in 1952 (68) to 96% in 1994 (58).
sentences.166: The omissions in death reporting and the late birth registrations affect mortali- ty rates, which will be biased up or down depending on whether birth or death omis- sions were higher.
sentences.167: However, given the much greater number of births than deaths, under- reporting of deaths will have a much greater effect on the rates.
sentences.168: In a study of 1976-1978 mortality by region, medical certification was used as an indirect measure of relative accuracy in the reporting of death (69,70).
sentences.169: Antofagasta and Valparaiso were among the few provinces with < 5% of deaths lacking medical certificates (69,70).
sentences.17: In the United States, it is estimated that 350,000 people obtain their drinking water from sources containing > 50 pg/L arsenic, the current maximum contaminant level (MCL) set by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) (12).
sentences.170: There is no evi- dence that underreporting was significantly different between the two study areas, but we did not find any published report with specific comparisons of fetal and infant mor- tality omissions by geographical locations across time.
sentences.171: In addition to the ecologic nature of the study and the potential effects of underascertainment of births or deaths, our analysis did not include other contaminants.
sentences.172: For exam- ple, differences in exposures to pesticides or other metals could have an effect on infant mortality.
sentences.173: Although we do not have specific information on pesticides, their use has been historically very limited in the Antofagasta region because it is a desert area with only local small-scale agriculture.
sentences.174: On the contrary, the Valparaiso region is one of the most pro- ductive agricultural areas of the country.
sentences.175: If pesticide exposure increased infant mortality, it would tend to increase the rates in Valparaiso so that the true RRs due to arsenic could be higher than those observed.
sentences.176: On the other hand, the Antofagasta region has a his- tory of mining and smelting that could have the opposite effect.
sentences.177: However, most exposed activities are not close to the city of Antofagasta.
sentences.178: Most importantly, it is unlikely that the clear sharp increase in arsenic water levels, followed by the decrease 12 years later with the installation of the arsenic-removal plant, would be accompanied by another contaminant with a similar temporal pattern.
sentences.18: Although higher exposures are more common in western states, recent concerns have also focused on other geographic regions where private well use is common.
sentences.180: Although there is suggestive evidence for arsenic-related human developmental toxici- ty, the existing literature falls short of establishing a clear causal association between environmental arsenic exposure and repro- ductive health effects.
sentences.181: The findings presented in this paper, albeit not definitive, support a role for arsenic in the increased late fetal and infant mortality observed in Antofagasta.
sentences.182: Further studies are needed to investigate the broad range of reproductive and develop- mental effects, ranging from low birth weight to infant death, that may be causally related to arsenic in environmentally exposed populations around the world.
sentences.183: The study designs of these investigations should consider using defined populations, with individual-level data and well-delineated methods of exposure assessment for arsenic and collection of data for potential confounding variables.
sentences.184: Results from the present study, the prospective cohort study under way in Chile by our group, and additional studies of this nature are important in the context of the ongoing review of the arsenic drinking water standard.

sentences.19: In areas where arsenic has been more extensively measured, levels are near the EPA MCL (12) or the World Health Organization rec- ommended guidance values of 10 pg/L (e.g., Minnesota, New Hampshire, and Michigan) (13)(14)(15).
sentences.2: Chronic arsenic exposure has been aociated with a range of neurologic, vascular, dermatologic, and carcinogenic effects.
sentences.20: Chronic arsenic exposure at high doses has neurologic, dermatologic, vascular, and carcinogenic effects (1, 2,16,17).
sentences.21: Exposure to arsenic from drinking water increases the risks of skin, lung, and bladder cancers (18)(19)(20), and also seems to be associated with diabetes (21,22).
sentences.22: The possible impact of arsenic on reproductive effects has been given less attention, but the collective evidence from human and laboratory studies suggests the potential for adverse effects on several reproductive end points.
sentences.23: Studies have reported adverse repro- ductive impacts among the offspring of employees and nearby residents of a Swedish copper smelter where arsenic exposures were documented (23)(24)(25)(26).
sentences.24: Female workers gave birth to lower weight infants than women who resided outside the smelter area, and the difference was greater if the mothers worked in highly exposed jobs (25).
sentences.25: An incremental trend in the rates of spontaneous abortions was observed with increasing occupational and residential exposure (24,25).
sentences.26: Congenital malformations appeared to be more frequent if the mother was employed in highly exposed jobs during pregnancy (26).
sentences.27: In Bulgaria, the incidence of toxemia of pregnancy and the mortality from congenital malformations were significantly higher than the national rates in an area near a smelter with environmental contamination from various metals (27).
sentences.28: A study in Texas found an increase in the rates of stillbirths in rela- tion to residential exposures from an arsenic pesticide factory (28).

state.hypothesis: Multi-walled carbon nanotube exposure causes macrophages to develop a mixed pro-inflammatory and profibrotic phenotype.

sentences.0: Background
sentences.1: The most common causes of granulomatous inflammation are persistent pathogens and poorly-degradable irritating materials.
sentences.10: Formation of multinucleated giant cells was also induced by asbestos fibers or MWCNTs in this 3D in vitro model.
sentences.100: Prior to exposure, single particles and well-dispersed asbestos fibers and carbon nanotubes are evident with minimal aggregation.
sentences.101: Following exposure to 0.5 μg/ml for 14 days in 3D cultures, limited agglomeration of carbon black particles is evident in comparison with submicron and micron-sized agglomerates of asbestos fibers and MWCNTs (Figure 9).
sentences.102: Discussion
sentences.103: This in vitro model of granuloma formation uses murine BMDM differentiated in vitro using macrophage colony stimulation factor (M-CSF) (Additional file 4 Table S1)
sentences.104: The phenotype of these differentiated cells resembles mature circulating blood monocytes (Additional file 4 Figure S1).
sentences.105: These cells are recruited into the lungs or the peritoneal cavity in response to particulate stimuli following an early influx of neutrophils.
sentences.106: If the particulate stimulus is toxic and biopersistent, these elicited macrophages may further differentiate into epithelioid macrophages and form a granuloma.
sentences.107: Activation of BMDM and formation of stable aggregates with the morphological features of a foreign body or non-immune granuloma are successfully reproduced in this serum-free, in vitro model only in response to high aspect ratio nanomaterials, not to spherical carbon black particles that have chemically similar surfaces, also composed of sp2-hybridized (graphenic) carbon.
sentences.108: The relative ranking of these materials for induction of granulomas in this 3D models is: MWCNT 3 > asbestos > MWCNT 1, MWCNT 2 > carbon back.
sentences.109: Surface area is not a major determinant of granuloma formation in this data set because the MWCNT 2 with a surface area of 200 m2/g did induce granuloma formation while carbon black nanoparticles with a surface area of 300 m2/g did not.
sentences.11: After 7-14 days, macrophages exposed to high aspect ratio nanomaterials co-expressed proinflammatory (M1) as well as profibrotic (M2) phenotypic markers.
sentences.110: Epithelioid granulomas are a prominent feature of the lung pathology induced in the first intratracheal instillation studies using carbon nanotubes.
sentences.111: Initially, this lesion was interpreted as an artifact due to bolus instillation of agglomerated carbon nanotubes.
sentences.112: Later studies using pharyngeal aspiration of SWCNTs also induced scattered foci of granulomatous inflammation as well as fibrosis.
sentences.113: This in vitro model of granuloma formation used well-dispersed samples of asbestos fibers and three commercial types of MWCNTs as illustrated in Figure 2.
sentences.114: Within 3-7 days after exposure, macrophages in 3D culture formed stable aggregates with the morphological features of an epithelioid granuloma.
sentences.115: These pathological lesions (Figure 10) are morphologically identical to granulomas induced in mice following pharyngeal aspiration of MWCNTs that are identical to sample 3 used in this in vitro model.
sentences.116: In this in vivo study, the MWCNTs were well-dispersed in synthetic lung lining fluid.
sentences.117: Ma-Hock et al. also delivered well-dispersed MWCNT to rats by inhalation and induced multifocal granulomas, even at a dose of 0.1 mg/m3 for 13 weeks.
sentences.118: During in vitro exposure in this 3D model, all of the nanomaterials underwent agglomeration (Figure 9), especially MWCNT 3 as illustrated in Figure 10.
sentences.119: This phenomenon may be driven by several events leading to entangled fibrous agglomerates that persist after the cells are lysed.
sentences.12: Conclusions
sentences.120: First, internalization of materials may lead to intracellular aggregation during phagocytosis.
sentences.121: Second, over time, macrophages may undergo repeated cycles of phagocytosis and cell death, resulting in extracellular release and accumulation of agglomerated fibrous nanomaterials.
sentences.122: High aspect ratio nanoparticles also induce frustrated phagocytosis and formation of multinucleated giant cells similar to the response of macrophages to asbestos fibers or carbon nanotubes following pharyngeal aspiration or intraperitoneal or pleural injection.
sentences.123: Similar to the study by Poland et al., this in vitro model used a range of commercial MWCNT samples with an iron content of < 0.1 - 1.8 wt-%; however, these samples induced granulomas to the same extent as crocidolite asbestos, the positive reference sample, with an iron content of 22%.
sentences.124: Porter et al. used the same MWCNT as our sample 3 and did not detect generation of hydroxyl radical using electron spin resonance (ESR).
sentences.125: Although redox activity of commercial carbon nanotubes is lower than that of amphibole asbestos fibers, this does not rule out a role for secondary generation of ROS by macrophages during phagocytosis of high aspect ratio nanomaterials.
sentences.126: The phenotype of BMDM induced by exposure of 3D cultures to asbestos fibers or MWCNTs also recapitulates the proinflammatory response of macrophages following inhalation of asbestos fibers.
sentences.127: For example, inhalation of chrysotile or crocidolite asbestos by rats increased formation of nitrotyrosine in alveolar macrophages and other target cells of the lungs and pleura suggesting induction of iNOS similar to this in vitro model.
sentences.128: Asbestos fibers delivered by inhalation to the lungs or by intraperitoneal injection to the mesothelium elicit an acute inflammatory response due to the proinflammatory mediators produced by resident macrophages.
sentences.129: Intratracheal instillation of asbestos fibers or MWCNTs in rats stimulated TNF-α release relative to ultrafine carbon black particles.
sentences.13: Induction of epithelioid granulomas appears to correlate with high aspect ratio and complex 3D structure of carbon nanotubes, not with their iron content or surface area.
sentences.130: In this in vitro model, asbestos fibers and MWCNTs also upregulated TNF-α protein expression in comparison to carbon black three days after exposure (Figure 7).
sentences.131: The proinflammatory mediators TNF-α, IL-1β, and iNOS have also been observed during the formation of immune granulomas in vivo  and in vitro .
sentences.132: Less is known about the mediators involved in production and healing of non-immune granulomas.
sentences.133: Non-immune or foreign body granulomas in the lung may progress to local fibrosis similar to the reaction to well-dispersed MWCNTs delivered to the lungs of rodents by pharyngeal aspiration.
sentences.134: The phenotype of activated macrophages in non-immune granulomas has not been characterized; however, arginase-1, a marker of M2 macrophage activation, is induced after 10-14 days following exposure to asbestos or MWCNTs in this in vitro model (Figure 8).
sentences.135: Induction of arginase-1 is associated with a profibrotic phenotype and may be useful as a biomarker to predict potential fibrosis induced by high aspect ratio nanoparticles.
sentences.136: Co-expression of proinflammatory as well as profibrotic phenotypic markers by epithelioid macrophages may be responsible for sustained inflammation and rapid development of fibrosis induced by MWCNTs in the lungs of rodents.
sentences.137: The biological mechanisms responsible for formation of stable aggregates of macrophages elicited from circulating blood monocytes in non-immune granulomas are unknown.
sentences.138: Differentiation of monocytes into epithelioid macrophages is a morphological feature of granulomas.
sentences.139: Epithelioid cells are large cells characterized by abundant endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria, lysosomes, and cytoplasmic vesicles and vacuoles.
sentences.14: This model offers a time- and cost-effective platform to evaluate the potential of engineered high aspect ratio nanomaterials, including carbon nanotubes, nanofibers, nanorods and metallic nanowires, to induce granulomas following inhalation.
sentences.140: Interdigititation of long, surface microvilli may be responsible for stable adhesion of epithelioid cells and they are the ultrastructural hallmark of granulomas; these morphological features are produced by exposure to asbestos fibers or MWCNTs, but not to carbon black (Figure 4).
sentences.141: The complex 3D aggregate structure (Figure 1C) characteristic of these commercial carbon nanotube samples may promote macrophage aggregation and granuloma formation in vitro and in vivo.
sentences.142: A major caveat in in vitro nanotoxicology assays is the high dose delivered to target cells that may not reflect human exposure under realistic conditions.
sentences.143: In this in vitro model, 1.4 × 105 BMDM were exposed to 0.05-0.5 μg of test particulates.
sentences.144: Elder et al. established a subchronic NOAEL for Printex 90, the carbon black sample used in this in vitro study, and determined that approximately 0.1 mg was deposited in the lungs of rats after 13 weeks inhalation at a dose of 1 mg/m3.
sentences.145: Assuming 3 × 107 alveolar macrophages per rat, the dose used in this in vitro assay is close to the deposited dose of carbon black under conditions that do not induce impaired clearance or inflammation.
sentences.146: For comparison, airborne dust levels of MWCNTs measured by Han et al. in a research facility were 400 μg/m3 and this dose corresponded to the doses delivered to mice by pharyngeal aspiration that produced lung granulomas and diffuse interstitial fibrosis.
sentences.147: Conclusion
sentences.148: The distinctive morphological and phenotypic responses of BMDM to reference particulates and MWCNTs in serum-free 3D culture establish proof-of-principle for this in vitro model as a potential alternative to both traditional 2D monolayer cultures and to rodent bioassays for granuloma formation.
sentences.149: This in vitro 3D model is a promising platform for testing of various commercial varieties of carbon nanotubes as well as other new high aspect ratio or one-dimensional nanomaterials including metallic nanowires, and ZnO or TiO2 nanorods and nanobelts
